The crude tanker rates may be marginally weaker, but not that much, maybe a little bit weaker than they were in the previous quarter, but again this is as of the last one week and this changes from day-to-day. Pritesh Chheda: And the bulk? G Shivakumar: Bulks have been getting much stronger in the last week

items.statement: Targeting 205,000-210,000 tons annual volume by FY28, implying ~15-20% volume CAGR over next 3-4 years
items.quote: We are confident that as we expand over the next 3 or 4 years, which is I believe we are targeting about 205,000 to 210,000 tons a year -- this year, which translates to around 15% to 20% growth.

items.statement: Awarded contract to Mott MacDonald for engineering consultancy to increase ABS capacity to 210 kt by FY28; debottlenecking to raise ABS from 85 kt to 105 kt and PS from 66 kt to 105 kt
items.quote: We have awarded a contract to M/s. Mott MacDonald Private Limited for engineering consultancy to increase the annual capacity of ABS production capacity to 210 kt by FY'28. We are also progressing as per schedule to increase our ABS capacity from 85 kt to 105 kt and PS capacity from 66 kt to 105 kt by various debottlenecking projects.

items.statement: INR 650 crore capex estimate for expansion is preliminary; detailed cost and timeline clarity expected in next couple of quarters after engineering studies
items.quote: The INR650 crores number was kind of a benchmark or kind of a rule of thumb number, which we have taken to get preliminary board approval to pursue engineering studies for the expansion, which is -- which we are undertaking.

items.statement: EBITDA margins stable at 12.2-12.4% in FY24; management believes current blended spreads are defendable and margins should improve with volume growth, product mix enrichment, and cost optimization
items.quote: Notably, PBITD margins were stable at 12.4% , previous quarter 12.3% for the quarter and 12.2% for the year, which is same as previous year driven by our debottlenecking efforts and an increased share of value -added products and cost optimization products.

items.statement: Specialty ABS grades ~60-65% of ABS volumes; developing value-added PS grades (refrigeration liner, high gloss, tint) and new blends (STYROLOY, ASALAC) to improve mix
items.quote: So it's around 60%-65%. It fluctuates again quarter-on-quarter. But on an annualized basis, you can consider that.

items.statement: Raw material cost pass-through via formula-based pricing with 1-2 month lag; margins well protected despite styrene monomer price increases
items.quote: Yes, that's right. So like I mentioned in previous calls, now this one is that a lot of our business is driven by fo rmulas as well. And in those formulas, we are able to pass on increases in raw material pricing to our customers fairly straightforward.

items.statement: Steam cost savings of INR 1.5-2 crore in last 5 months at Nandesari plant (~INR 4 crore annualized); similar projects underway at Dahej and Katol; pursuing wind-solar hybrid power PPAs for power cost reduction
items.quote: If you look at power and fuel, for instance, and specifically in fuel, we already have incorporated certain systems in our Nandesari plant wherein in terms of the steam co sts in the last 5 months or so w e have seen a saving of close to INR1.5 crores to INR2 crores, just in the steam cost, which, on an annualized basis, probably is going to be more than INR4 crores, just on fuel cost in one of ou

items.statement: Domestic ABS capacity expected to exceed 400 kt by FY27 and 450 kt by FY28 vs ~300 kt currently; management believes market will remain underserved given 7-10% demand growth
items.quote: Even then we believe that in the next 4 years, the capacity from 300,000 tons which is actually slightly higher than 300,000 tons this year fr om what we have gathered data on, we'll exceed 400,000 tons in year '26-'27 and probably go to 450,000 tons in '27-'28.

items.statement: ABS market share increased from ~26-27% to ~30%; PS market share increased from ~17% to ~20%; focusing on OEM engagement for PS contractual business
items.quote: So last year, I think in ABS, we had about 26% or 27% market share. And in PS, our market share was closer to around 17%.

items.statement: Exports not a priority currently; 50% of ABS demand met by imports, focus on capturing domestic market first; open to selective export opportunities if value-accretive
items.quote: So in terms of overall volume growth, we are still looking first to satisfy our existing customers and only then look at exports as a proposition. We have a strong brand positioning also in the Indian market. So it beh oves us first to look at that as an opportunity and only then pursue other opportunities once we have additional capacity already in place.

items.statement: FY24 sales volume 165 kt (+10.7% YoY); Q4 FY24 volume up 25% QoQ; revenue INR 2,222 crore; PBITDA INR 273 crore
items.quote: Our sales volume grew by 10.7% Y -o-Y to 165 kt for the financial year 2024 and by 25% compared to the preceding quarter.

items.statement: China's ABS self-sufficiency and new Asian capacities already creating pricing pressure; normalized margin environment post-COVID; competitive intensity may increase with domestic capacity additions
items.quote: Post -COVID, China did not come back as strongly as was earlier anticipated. There were also new capacities which have come on in China. So there has been a fair amount of pricing pressure from countries like I mentioned, in the case of ABS would have in Korea, Thailand, Taiwan, etc.

items.statement: Agrawal family management took control in November 2022; strategic focus on capacity augmentation, cost rationalization, new products, sustainability, and culture
items.quote: As you know that our management took over the company only in November '22. So it's been about 16 -odd months that we have had management control over the company. And in this time is when we realized, and we announced plans to go ahead with expansion.

items.statement: Power policy clarity awaited for wind-solar hybrid PPAs; Gujarat policy clauses still pending government clearance; state-level approvals affect power cost savings timeline
items.quote: While it's happened in Gujarat as well, but there are certain clauses which still have to be completely cleared by the government. So in any case, that should be done soon and we believe that will add to our kind of power saving as well.

items.statement: No specific working capital metrics discussed; focus on cost optimization in logistics expected to yield savings next year
items.quote: There are other projects as well, which are in logistics and other areas, which will also lead to significant savings. But currently, it's hard to exactly estimate. I think, we will see the impact of at least some of these things in specifically in power and fuel in this year, in the full year that we see and more so in the next couple of quarters a nd for logistics, you will see in the following

items.statement: FY25 EBITDA margin guidance of 15% for full year and 18% exit rate in Q4 FY25
items.quote: my guidance for the current year is 15% for EBITDA and for next year it is around 18%.

items.statement: FY25 gross margin guidance of 52% to 53%
items.quote: FY25 should be 52% to 53%.

items.statement: Target to reduce net borrowing to around Rs. 250 crore by end of FY25
items.quote: My net borrowing today is Rs. 485 crore, which we are looking to make it half of what it is, around Rs.250 crore.

items.statement: Aim to reduce total inventory to around Rs. 200 crore by end of FY25 from Rs. 900 crore currently
items.quote: by end of the year we are looking at reducing our inventory close to Rs. 200 crore

items.statement: Q4 FY24 gross margin was 50%, down due to lower Bangladesh share; standalone gross margin flat
items.quote: Gross margin for this quarter was 50%, I know it's not encouraging, but there is no discounting in this. What has happened actually is the share of business from Bangladesh has reduced and 5% of the impact on gross margin is mainly because of that.

items.statement: Q4 FY24 EBITDA margin 2.3% includes Rs. 15 crore one-offs (Rs. 5 crore employee cost, rest legal/professional fees)
items.quote: EBITDA 2.3% there are some one offs. Close to Rs. 15 crore is mainly because of one offs which will not be there as we move going forward.

items.statement: Hard luggage capacity to increase from 10 lakh to 13 lakh pieces by end of FY25; soft luggage capacity at 7 lakh pieces
items.quote: 10 and 7 for soft luggage, 2 to 3 lakh we are going to increase in hard luggage at this point of time.

items.statement: EBO refurbishment budget of Rs. 10-12 crore for FY25 covering multiple stores at Rs. 30-40 lakh each
items.quote: We have a budget of around Rs. 10 - Rs. 12 crore for the year to do that.

items.statement: Plan to add only 35-40 EBOs in FY25, focus on optimizing throughput of existing 507 EBOs
items.quote: in FY25 we are not going to add too many EBOs we are looking at only close to. Manish Desai: 35 to 40 EBOs, but more strategy will be to leverage on the existing strength what we have and to optimize the throughput

items.statement: Confident of double-digit revenue growth in FY25 based on industry growth of 12% and market share gains; travel indicators positive
items.quote: we feel that by doing right we will start to gain market share and if the industry is growing, and most of the people are saying that the industry will grow 12% and that is the confidence I am getting, I should do 1% or 2% better than industry and that's how I'm saying that we should do a double digit growth.

items.statement: Premium/mid-premium brands (VIP, Skybags, Carlton) at 55% of business; target to increase to 60%; Carlton at 6% targeting 10%
items.quote: business is coming from other than Aristocrat which is mid premium and premium. Overall market in India is close to Rs.1000 crore, maybe 20% market is premium. My idea is that if overall today we are at 55 % how can we make this 60% that will definitely give us an uptick on the improvement in margins

items.statement: Aristocrat crossed Rs. 1,000 crore revenue in FY24; Caprese crossed Rs. 100 crore; new launches in lightweight, sustainability, premium hard luggage in April
items.value: Rs. 1,000 crore Aristocrat, Rs. 100 crore Caprese
items.quote: segments , so Aristocrat actually touched a Rs. 1000 crore club in this year . On Premiumization side, Carlton did very well it grew however VIP and Skybags some more work to do. Caprese also

items.quote: Not really. 50% of our trolleys act ually have already become MS steel. It's become fungible now, and overall trolley cost as a percentage of the luggage is not substantial to make a dent into the profitability

items.statement: Soft luggage inventory of Rs. 300 crore (6 months stock) selling at Rs. 50 crore/month; strict RM ordering controls requiring MD/CFO sign-off
items.quote: Out of the Rs. 900 crore of inventory close to Rs. 300 odd crore is mainly soft luggage and we have stopped producing soft luggage upright and every month we are selling around Rs. 50 crore worth of soft luggage inventory, it is a six month of inventory.

items.statement: Hard luggage inventory lean at ~15 days; RM ordering for soft luggage frozen until inventory drops to 2-3 lakh pieces
items.quote: In hard luggage actually we are not having much inventory it's generally 15 days or even 15 days of inventory is not there today, as we speak and soft luggage now , any RM ordering actually requires a signature from CFO or MD otherwise it's a clear, clear zero ordering.

items.statement: Insurance refund for Bangladesh factory fire expected around Q2 FY25; EPZ unit permissions causing delay
items.quote: We should see something around quarter two.

items.statement: Bangladesh workforce reduced by 4,000 people; retaining skilled labor for 75,000-80,000 soft luggage capacity
items.quote: We have already cut costs o f 4000 people to take care of only the relevant demand, but I don't want to reduce further because then I will not get the skilled labor which I need to manufacture this 75,000 pieces

items.statement: E-commerce grew 143% in Q4 FY24; now 22% of sales targeting industry level of 25%; offline general trade also growing
items.quote: e-commerce channel continued in the growth trajectory it actually grew more than nine months, so we grew 14 3% in the quart er four for e-commerce.

items.statement: Channel margin ranking: retail/EBO highest, then general trade, then modern trade and e-commerce lowest, CSD close to retail
items.quote: retail trade is the best margin contributor followed by GT, modern trade and e-commerce are the lowest, CSD is also close to retail. MT and e-commerce go hand in hand with lower margins.

items.statement: Skybags positioned mid-premium not opening price point; channel partner discounting corrected after brand intervention
items.quote: Skybags strategy is definitely more with mid premium and not opening price point. This particular range what you are seeing, I know why and that was mainly because the channel partner sold at lower than what price we sold them so that was their investment and not ours, and we have actually asked them to increase the price because that's also hurting my brand and secondly, it's also hurting my othe

items.statement: High inventory (Rs. 900 crore) and debt (Rs. 485 crore) create vulnerability if FY25 demand forecast of 12% industry growth fails
items.quote: we understand we have a high inventory and high debt both go hand in hand and all our efforts are on to reduce this so, reduce both borrowings as well as reduce inventory.

items.statement: Bangladesh utilization improvement expected from Q3 FY25 as soft luggage inventory depletes by September; backpack/duffel expansion to follow
items.quote: A large part of utilization of Bangladesh improvement you will start to see from quarter three.

items.statement: Management expects revenue and profit to improve in FY25 but declines to give specific numeric targets
items.quote: We are working extremely hard, and they have reasons to believe in either case, we will be better off in this election year than what we were later or last to last year.

items.statement: Animal healthcare industry grows at 8-9%; Hester grew 12% standalone and aims to maintain or exceed that rate
items.quote: Animal healthcare industry itself grows at a rate of 8% to 9%. We have grown at a 12% standalone basis. So, I think I mean this is the yardstick which is Hester Biosciences Limited 10 May 2024 there and now we either maintain it or get better, these are the only two options

items.statement: Company repaid Rs. 30 crores of debt in FY24 and plans to repay Rs. 25-30 crores annually
items.quote: Almost we have around Rs. 25-Rs. 30 crores of debt, we get paid on an annual basis.

items.statement: BSL-3 facility repurposing permission expected shortly; fill-finish line near completion and should go on stream in next two months
items.quote: The BSL-3 facility we have asked for purposing it from COVID other vaccine , we will get permission of that shortly or already working, or trying to get into other animal vaccines, and so that will be online, and fill-finish is near to complete and that should go on stream in the next two months' time.

items.statement: Nepal plant turnover Rs. 13.5 crores in FY24 with capacity to do more than double, potentially three times current turnover
items.quote: We did a turnover of Rs. 13 crores. Now, even at this rate, we still have more than double the capacity, three times rather we can do turnover in our Nepal plant from where we are.

items.statement: Poultry industry on upswing; farmers moving to progressive farming and increasing vaccine uptake
items.quote: The poultry industry is now definitely on an upswing. And this upswing makes move towards a more a progressive way of poultry farming. And yes, there is going to be an improvement on their pickup for vaccines, etc., and I am sure this is now going to continue for sure.

items.statement: Feed ingredient prices stable, poultry demand okay, disease incidence low, and government allowing avian influenza vaccine production — all positive indicators for poultry sector
items.quote: The poultry infected by feed prices, right now the ingredient prices are even okay. The demand for overall poultry is okay as our economy is doing good . Disease incidences are less at this point of time plus the Government of India has also allowed that the production of the Avian influenza vaccines, which will be launched not only by us , by other companies as well in the next 3 to 8 months, so

items.statement: Hester Nepal executed FAO tender for PPR vaccine and anticipates it to carry forward this year
items.quote: Hester Nepal executed FAO tender for the P PR vaccine and anticipating this to carry forward this year.

items.statement: Hester Africa achieved Rs. 5.2 crores topline in FY24 and is well prepared for anticipated government orders in FY25, focusing on East and Central African countries
items.quote: Hester Africa is also well prepared to meet the anticipated government orders in the coming financial year, with the primary focus on serving the East and Central African countries.

items.statement: Q4 profit margins increased due to strategic product mix; EBITDA and PAT growth closely aligned with enhanced sales performance
items.quote: Our profit margins have increased primarily attributed to a strategic share product mix. Furthermore, both EBITDA and PAT missed a growth closely aligning with our enhanced sales performance.

items.statement: Margins will shift depending on product mix; company wants to focus more on health products alongside vaccines in coming years
items.quote: So, to answer your question, I think yes, the margins will sort of shift depending on the product mix, but in the coming years, we definitely want to also focus more on health.

items.statement: Lumpy skin disease vaccine development underway using technology from ICAR; dedicated vaccine expected ready by next year when government starts buying again
items.quote: Our developmental activity hopefully next year, around this time when the government starts again buying the vaccine, we should be ready before that for the dedicated lumpy skin disease vaccine.

items.quote: So, sir, if we see there has been a net loss of Rs. 18 crores for the year, but if you look at the EBITDA numbers, we are positive, almost Rs. 1.5 crore EBITDA positive. items.statement: Working with insurance companies and distributors to address dairy sector demand from cattle insurance-linked vaccination; process evolving slowly due to fragmented dairy farmer base
items.quote: We had a meeting with an insurance company, which came to mee t us to even talk this about all these things, so that how do they take it and h ow does the cattle farmer get the vaccine, etc. It is something which is an organic thing, which is happening right now, it is an evolution.

items.statement: Global PPR eradication program led by FAO; funding improving slowly; meetings held annually with next in September; no specific order visibility or financial data available
items.quote: The global PPR eradication program as you know has been spearheaded by United Nations Food and Agriculture Organization. And they in turn depend upon funding from countries, which slowly is now improving what it was in the last 2-3 years and while there are no indications given to us or to any other manufacturer, to put on record every year, there are one or two meetings that are conducted . Anoth

items.statement: Cash flows for FY24 showed improvement, marking a positive trajectory
items.quote: I am also pleased to highlight there are cash flows for the current year have shown improvement, marking a positive trajectory.

items.statement: Nepal subsidiary started paying income tax for the first time, indicating progress
items.quote: Our debt has gone, now more or less it is a very small debt that in fact we have already started paying income tax over there. This is the first time. So, that shows a sign of progress.

items.statement: Quarterly turnover including GST exceeded Rs.100 crores for Q4 FY24.
items.quote: We are very happy to inform you that quarterly turnover including G ST is more than Rs.100,00,00,000 quarterly more than Rs.100 crores.

items.statement: Full year FY24 volume reached 57,229 tonnes, up from 54,230 tonnes in FY23.
items.quote: Yes, Vikram we have just to tell you, for the full year volume in the tonnage , in the tonnage is there of the Rs.57,229 is the tonnage volume for the full year Rs.57,229.

items.statement: Domestic volume grew 2-3% to 49,662 tonnes in FY24 from 48,447 tonnes in FY23.
items.quote: In the domestic we are able to increase from Rs.48,447 of the last year to Rs.49,662 that's domestic.

items.statement: International volume growth drove overall volume increase as domestic growth was muted due to receivables caution.
items.quote: Internationally is one of the thing it can trigger up. We are a little bit cautious in case of the domestic for this year, which is expected to improve in future but this year we have been cautious considering the receivables only, we were a little cautious.

items.statement: EBITDA margin for the asset-light air freight business is around 4% to 5%.
items.quote: I can talk about our business where we are not owning the aircraft and there is a EBITDA of generally what we are earning is around near to the 4% to 5%.

items.statement: Variable cost component ATF is passed on to customers in real time; contracts are open, not fixed.
items.quote: We basically have our main component, or the variable cost is aviation turbine fuel , ATF, if ATF prices are increasing or decreasing, we pass on to consumer , customer I mean to say. So, we don't get affected by the variation in the oil prices as you can see in the international.

items.statement: Trade payables credit period is 90 to 120 days per industry practice; receivables insured via SBI Life; no bill discounting due to surplus cash.
items.quote: Yes. So, there is a normal industry practice of let say 90 to 120 days.

items.statement: Company became net debt free after repaying public fixed deposits and long-term borrowings; closing cash balance Rs.17.49 crores.
items.quote: As a result, the Company had become net debt free and Company is carrying a closing balance of cash and cash equivalent of Rs.17,49,00,000.

items.statement: Sold Chennai land; exploring warehouse development in Pune with proceeds; Bangalore property yields Rs.4-5 lakh monthly rent.
items.value: Rs.4 to Rs.5 lakh per month
items.quote: Rental is around Rs.4 to Rs.5 lakh.

items.statement: Actively exploring both inorganic and organic growth opportunities beyond aviation, including roadways (Patel Roadways legacy).
items.quote: So, we are actively looking for the opportunity both inorganic and organic to grow the business, to expand the Company.

items.statement: Pricing environment hardening due to Red Sea crisis shifting cargo to air routes; expect momentum to continue into FY25.
items.quote: Vikram the prices are getting harder definitely as our Red Sea crises and all the other crises happen. So, definitely because what is happening is ocean routes are not available then people have to go for the air route.

items.statement: Expect to maintain Q4 FY24 quarterly turnover momentum of Rs.101 crores including GST into FY25.
items.quote: We expect to keep the momentum for us as a Company also, the numbers which we have in the quarter gone by . We expect to keep that momentum.

items.statement: Government airport expansion to 240 by 2030, Rs.30,000 crore capex over 5 years, and 1000 UDAN routes to boost logistics sector.
items.quote: the airport authority of India planned capital expenditure of 30,000 crore over five years and the government's target of 1000 UDAN routes, to create 1000 UDAN routes will further boost the expansion of logistic into new territories.

items.statement: Tie-ups with all major airlines (IndiGo, Vistara, Air India, SpiceJet, Akasa) mitigate pilot strike risk; no single airline dependency.
items.quote: We have a tie up starting from Indigo, Vistara, Air India, SpiceJet, whatever name Akasa airline, we have a tie up with all the airlines so our operation don't get affected by this strike.

items.statement: Trade receivables insured with SBI Life to cover unfortunate events; no bill discounting currently.
items.quote: we have taken insurance also for our trade receivable from the SBI life. So, if any unfortunate events happen, then they can get the backup from the insurance Company, that we have done.

items.statement: Promoters fully subscribed and oversubscribed in previous two rights issues demonstrating commitment.
items.quote: promoters have shown their commitment, they have fully contributed, contributed more than what was required of their eligible contributors.

items.statement: Khar property attracting interest from big brand for operation; discussions ongoing, details not disclosed.
items.quote: now good interest from the big brand for operating that property. But further details cannot be shared at this stage and discussion stage.

items.statement: Q4 FY24 volume grew 7% YoY and 30% QoQ; FY24 net sales fell 4.3% to INR 669.4 cr with 2% volume decline
items.quote: These efforts started paying off with a quarter 4 showing a 7% volume growth and a 3.7% value growth. For the full year, your company registered net sales of INR 669.4 crores as against INR 699.6 crores in FY23, a drop of 4.3% and a volume drop of 2%.

items.statement: Reported EBITDA margin 5.9% in Q4 FY24; like-for-like EBITDA margin 8.1% vs 7.1% YoY excluding brand spend
items.quote: EBITDA margins on a like-for-like basis, when I say so, I exclude the additional investments that we continue to support the brand expense which is the new TVC. This was 8.1% versus 7.1% Y-o-Y while the reported EBITDA is obviously a little lower at 5.9% margins.

items.statement: Achieved ~3.5% YoY production cost savings on like-for-like basis; gas prices stable sequentially, raw materials softening
items.quote: We continued the drive to optimize our production costs and we achieved a savings of roughly 3.5% Y-o-Y on a like-for-like basis which is at constant product mix and energy cost.

items.statement: GVT share in sales mix rose to 30% in FY24 from 23% in FY23; vitrified-ceramic split now 50-50
items.quote: On the positive side, gas prices also cooled down and this push on retail market through the year has helped us to grow our share of glazed vitrified tiles in the company's sales mix to 30% versus 23% for FY23.

items.statement: Commissioned Dora GVT line (3.3 msqm/yr) ahead of schedule at 18% lower capex; FY24 capex-to-revenue >10%
items.quote: The company commissioned its Dora plant GVT line, the second GVT line with a capacity of 3.3 million square meter annually ahead of schedule and also at a reduced capex cost of about 18%.

items.statement: Dora GVT line ramping up, full utilization expected in ~1 year; overall GVT utilization 75-80% in FY24; associate Proton adding 5.5 msqm GVT in Q2 FY25
items.quote: Our associate company in Morbi will also be launching a new line in quarter two with a 5.5 million square meter capacity which will also be available to us to feed the market.

items.statement: Private project order book healthy; government project order book lower due to elections, expected to pick up from Q2 FY25
items.quote: I think the order book on private projects is healthy. The order book on government projects is lesser than what I would want it to be. But as I said, quarter four has been a bit slow on the government front because of elections and all. And we expect that to start picking up from quarter two onwards.

items.statement: Project sales (orders >3,000 sqm) contributed ~25% of FY24 revenue; retail ~75% (including 12% via dealers)
items.quote: Anything which is more than 3,000 meters single location is what we call a project. This contribution was about 25% for the full year. 25% for the full year was split for project versus what we do directly through the enterprise piece.

items.statement: Core cash conversion cycle maintained at 19 days despite higher credit and inventory to support sales
items.quote: Despite supporting sales via higher credit inventory, we still insured an overall healthy core cash conversion cycle at 19 days.

items.statement: Net debt INR 27.5 cr (lower than Dec 2023); new term loan for Dora GVT line, repayments start FY25
items.quote: The net debt is only INR27.5 crores which is in fact lower than what we had in December '23. The gross debt obviously represents the new term loan that has been drawn to fund the Dora new GVT line and the repayments for this will commence only from next fiscal.

items.statement: Board recommended 5% dividend for FY24
items.quote: The Board has also therefore recommended a 5% dividend for the last fiscal.

items.statement: No formal volume guidance; brand spend to continue at 3-5% of revenue through FY25; TV campaign active till mid-June 2024
items.quote: I think 3% to 5% is on an average what we have been spending now for the past few quarters. And I think that should be the broader thing that would be there for the next few quarters as well.

items.statement: Morbi exports fell from ~INR 2,000 cr/month in H1 to INR 1,500-1,600 cr/month in H2; ~50% of 1,000+ units shut in April; US anti-dumping investigation risk
items.quote: And I think exports within H1 were moving towards almost, you know, moving towards INR 2,000 crores a month kind of a figure. As in H2, my estimate is would have come down to about INR1,500 crores-INR1,600 crores a month kind of a number.

items.statement: US actively considering anti-dumping duty on Indian tiles; investigations ongoing
items.quote: plus there is now the news on US actively considering putting a dumping duty on Indian tiles. There are some investigations which are going there which is also a bit of a dampener going forward.

items.statement: Average gas price ~INR 50/scm for FY24; blended with AFR reduces by INR 6-7; spot prices low but linkage benefit uncertain
items.quote: For the full year, obviously, it is much lower than the last year. You can say an average of 50 across locations. This is only gas without counting in the blessings on the AFR front. If you take that into consideration, on a blended basis, reduce it by INR6-INR7.

items.statement: Morbi functional capacity estimated at 9 cr sqm/month ceramics + 9 cr sqm/month vitrified (~2 bn sqm/yr total industry capacity)
items.quote: So, the capacity which is functional today, our estimate is that it was 9 crores square meters a month of ceramics and another 9 crores a month of vitrified. This is what the functional capacity we estimated in the month of April.

items.statement: Export pressure from Red Sea shipping costs and US anti-dumping probe; Morbi overcapacity keeping pricing under pressure
items.quote: Because of issues in the Red Sea, the sink rates going up, insurance charges going up, plus there is now the news on US actively considering putting a dumping duty on Indian tiles.

items.statement: Added 17 new exclusive display centers (Orient Bell Tile Boutique) in FY24
items.quote: The company has also added 17 new exclusive display centers, the Orient Bell Tile Boutique as we call it, in FY'24.

items.statement: Associate Proton expanding 5.5 msqm GVT capacity in Q2 FY25 funded by internal accruals, no equity support from OBL
items.quote: By the way, just for you and of records, they are doing it out of their own internal accruals. We are not paying out any money to them. So there is no equity support from OBL.

items.statement: Granted first patent for antimicrobial/antiviral tile method; targeting hospital projects in FY25 for differentiation
items.quote: During this year, the company has also been granted a first-ever patent for the unique method of preparing an antimicrobial and antiviral tile. This is something which we will be using in FY'25 to win project orders in the health sector.

items.statement: Management expects double-digit revenue growth in FY25 and aims to sustain it for the next two to three years.
items.quote: We are expecting a double digit growth this year.

items.statement: Management targets EBITDA margins of 15-16% for FY25.
items.quote: Around 15%-16% EBITDA you can expect.

items.statement: FY24 EBITDA margin improved 188 bps to 14% due to softening raw material prices partially offset by higher fixed costs.
items.quote: EBITDA margin was at 14%, improved by 188 basis points year-on-year as against 12.1% in FY23.

items.statement: Gross margins expected to sustain at 58-60% going forward.
items.quote: So we can expect like 58%-60% of gross margins going forward, I believe

items.statement: Pricing strategy depends on input costs; prices to remain stable if inputs are stable, with focus on competitiveness.
items.quote: The pricing depends upon our cost of the inputs. If the input remains stable, then prices also remain stable.

items.statement: Realizations will not decrease and are expected to improve for both open and closed footwear.
items.quote: Realization is not going to come down. It will only improve.

items.statement: Open footwear volume grew significantly in FY24; closed footwear faced oversupply from new entrants over last two years.
items.quote: This performance was largely driven by a significant uptick in open footwear volume s, a witness to the efficacy of our strategic initiatives to regain market

items.statement: Closed footwear demand was weak due to oversupply; consolidation expected but timing depends on market forces.
items.quote: A l ot of new entrants have come in the market and the price what they are offering. But there's more supply than demand in the last 2 years

items.statement: Rural demand expected to pick up with good monsoon; sports footwear purchases delayed due to high inflation last year.
items.quote: Going forward we are expecting good monsoon and the demand should definitely uptake.

items.statement: Overall capacity utilization at 65%; closed footwear utilization at 55%; Sparx utilization at 55-60%.
items.quote: Capacity utilization is around 65%.

items.statement: 30-acre land parcel acquired in Bhiwadi for Rs 127 crore for future greenfield expansion; no immediate capacity addition needed.
items.quote: we have land in our hand. So whenever we want to increase productio n, then we have to start the process of building the factory because we are always having greenfield projects

items.statement: FY24 capex of Rs 248 crore included Rs 127 crore for land, Rs 30-40 crore for moulds, and balance for plant, machinery and buildings.
items.quote: In FY24, the company incurred a total CapEx of Rs. 248 crores, including a purchase of 30-acre land parcel i n Bhiwadi, Rajasthan, worth Rs. 127 crores

items.statement: All-time high annual volume of 19.5 crore pairs sold in FY24, driven by open footwear.
items.quote: We have sold maximum number of pairs. We have touched 19.5 crores pairs, that is all-time high.

items.statement: Revenue mix: Relaxo+Bahamas 25%, Flite 37%, Sparx 38%; open footwear 80%, closed 20% of total revenue.
items.quote: Relaxo with Bahamas, 25%. And then Sparx and Flite both are equal, so 25% Relaxo plus Bahamas and rest 50-50 Sparx and Flite.

items.statement: Management expects open:closed mix to shift from 80:20 to 75:25 over time.
items.quote: Right now it is 80% is open and 20% is closed. So we are expecting that 75: 25 it will become.

items.statement: Retailer app launched; 50,000 outlets downloaded; target to reach 1 lakh outlets in FY25 for better demand forecasting and engagement.
items.quote: we have launched the app. So this is a retailer app. We are doing engagement with the retailer now. So with the help of the app, we are able to touch 50,000

items.statement: EBO count at 400+; plan to add 50-60 more in FY25.
items.quote: We currently have more than 400. We're going to add 50-60 more outlets.

items.statement: Competitive intensity high in closed footwear due to new entrants offering higher credit and discounts; open footwear less affected.
items.quote: Majorly in closed footwear.

items.statement: Exports contribute ~4.5% of turnover; traction across Africa, Gulf, Central America, Oceania; margins similar to domestic due to government incentives.
items.quote: We are around 4.5% of footwear company turnover in exports.

items.statement: Receivables increased ~30% in FY24 due to subdued demand and slow payments from trade.
items.quote: This has increased because there is a pressure in the market. The demand is subdued. So because of pressure in the market, there is an increase of the outstanding.

items.statement: Company remains net debt-free supported by positive operating cash flow.
items.quote: We remain a net debt-free company supported by a positive cash from operations.

items.statement: BIS/QCO implemented; moderate cost increase passed on; micro and small enterprises exempted creating uneven playing field.
items.quote: As per the rule, government has exempted micro and small from this implementation of QCO. It is only on medium and large industry.

items.statement: A&P spend at 9% of sales (4-4.5% advertising, rest schemes); plan to maintain same percentage in FY25.
items.quote: So if you talk about A&SP, so it is roughly around, for advertisement, we do around 4%-4.5%. And the rest is the schemes and that, both put together comes to 9%.

items.statement: E-commerce contributes 9-10% of total sales; shift to Brand-as-Seller model to control pricing.
items.quote: We do roughly around 9% to 10% in e-commerce of our total sales.

items.statement: Natural rubber sourced domestically; polymers imported from multiple countries (not China); supply chain stable.
items.quote: The material, natural rubber, we are sourcing here in India itself and the other polymers like they're being imported.

items.statement: Raw material volatility (EVA, LDPE, PVC) impacted profitability in recent years; future volatility unpredictable.
items.quote: Because we talk about EVA from Rs. 120 per kg, it went to Rs. 300. And this is short span, it came down to Rs. 150-Rs. 120 again. That kind of volatility we've never seen in the past.

items.statement: Employee and operating costs grew 13% and 16% in FY24 due to increments and headcount additions despite low revenue growth.
items.quote: There is no exception because revenue has not grown as expenses has grown. So in cases implied, definitely, there is an increment and adding of some people also.

items.statement: Completed Rs 1,000 crore QIP fundraise in April 2024 with marquee institutional investors
items.quote: I'm happy to share that we have successfully completed Rs.1,000 crores QIP fundraise in April 24 by onboarding marquee institutional investors who will partner with us on the exciting journey ahead

items.statement: Reduced net debt by Rs 334 crore in FY24 through internal cash generation
items.quote: I am glad to share that our cash generation from the business helped us reduce our net debt by Rs.334 crores during FY24.

items.statement: Divested holdings in M B Manshaan for Euro 5.95 million in FY24
items.quote: In FY24 we divested our holdings in M B Manshaan for Euro 5.95 million.

items.statement: No specific FY25 guidance given; will provide guidance once demand normalizes and utilization reaches 70-80%
items.quote: No, currently we are not looking to give any specific guidance, because we are still in that phase as I have been sharing that principally, in our optical business we have made all the right investments in our capacities, in our team product capability, but our utilization levels are still on the lower side.

items.statement: Optical business utilization at sub-50% in Q4 FY24; break-even at 60-65% utilization
items.quote: We won't give specific numbers Ashish for competitive reasons, but it was sub 50% levels.

items.statement: Open order book at Rs 10,290 crore end of Q4 FY24 with Rs 2,064 crore added in Q4
items.quote: Our open order book at the end of Q4 FY24 is Rs.10,290 crores we are happy to share that robust order book edition amounting to Rs.2,064 crores happened during last quarter.

items.statement: Expect inventory normalization in 1-2 quarters; demand recovery visible from Q3/Q4 FY25 with BEAD contribution meaningful in FY26
items.quote: So that's where we stand today. There are efforts going on locally in the US around how the timing can be fast track but currently, the visibility is probably Q 3/Q4 of our financial year, is where we can see some initial impact or benefit and then meaningfully next year

items.statement: Global Services EBITDA margin improved to 12.1% in Q4 FY24 and 7.6% for full year; target 8-10% sustainable range
items.quote: We have been selective in our intake and execution which has helped us improve our Q 4 EBIT DA to Rs.39 crores and EBITDA margin to healthy 12.1

items.statement: Optical connectivity attach rate increased to 13% from 10% in FY24; first connectivity sales in North America
items.quote: Our optical connectivity attach rates have increased to 13% from 10% last year.

items.statement: Global OFC demand projected at 617M fiber-km by 2026 and 666M by 2028 (4.4% CAGR); ex-China ~8% CAGR
items.quote: As we look at the future projections from CRU, the medium term demand for optical fiber cable volumes is expected to go up to 617 million fiber kilometers by 2026 and 666 million fiber kilometers by 202 8, up from 536 million kilometers in CY2023, this is a healthy 4.4% annual growth rate from 2023 to 2028 and approximately 8% annual growth excluding China

items.statement: Anti-dumping duties on Chinese products in India and Europe expected to benefit non-Chinese players like STL
items.quote: The application of anti-dumping duty on Chinese products in India, Europe is expected to balance out the optical connectivity product supply and help non Chinese players such as STL further standing up our global positioning.

items.statement: Completed capex cycle with operationalization of US facility; now set up to fulfill US-made optic fiber cable demand
items.quote: During the FY24 we also completed our capex cycle with the operationalization of our US facility and we are now fully set up to fulfill demands of US made optic fiber cable products.

items.statement: Reduced permanent employee costs significantly; contract labor costs reported under other expenses; some cost to return as optical interconnect capability builds
items.quote: So, with respect to the e mployee cost, if you see the manpower cost, it's all about the permanent employees. While the labor costs which is generally it's a contract labor, which is not part of the manpower cost, it's getting reported as the other expenses are part of the line

items.statement: No election impact seen in India or US; BEAD funding bipartisan and election-resilient
items.quote: No, we are not seeing any impact of the elections per se whether in India or globally.

items.statement: Realizations reasonably stable in recent quarters; no reduction seen in focus markets; pricing varies by geography
items.quote: I would at least comment that in the last couple of quarters the market has been fairly stable and at least from our focus markets, we don't see any reduction in realization.

items.statement: Focus on right cash profile projects in Services to reduce fund involvement; working capital optimization ongoing
items.quote: We have been very focused on taking on the right kind of projects with the right margins and most importantly right cash profile to reduce our fund involvement so that efforts continue.

items.statement: Market share at 8% global cable demand ex-China in FY24; expected to normalize as fresh demand picks up
items.quote: Basis CRU global consumption data during FY24 we had 8% market share and global cable demand excluding China.

items.statement: Revenue mix diversifying towards North America and Europe as optical demand picks up globally
items.quote: On the back of our global businesses our revenue mix was well diversified during last quarter and we expect this to further improve towards North America and Europe as the demand for the optical products pick up in the global markets.

items.statement: UK services business nearly at breakeven with good order flow
items.quote: And one more thing to add is that we also had in line with what we had promised, we have been able to get our UK services nearly to breakeven so I think that is also something that's positive and we see good order flow up there.

items.statement: Demerger of services business: first NCLT hearing held April 2024; directed to convene shareholder/creditor meetings for scheme approval
items.quote: During the quarter, the first NCLT hearing was conducted in April 2024 NCLT has directed us to convene the meeting of the shareholders secured and unsecured creditors to approve the scheme of demerger and we are working on next steps in the approval process.

items.statement: FY25 credit growth guidance of 10% minimum, confident of achieving around 12%
items.quote: Earlier also we had given 10% and you can see that we have grown 11.34% even after rejigging the pricing of the corporate portfolio. And this year also what we have given, 10%, is a minimum growth. And we are sure 3 that we will grow around 12% in the current financial year

items.statement: FY24 NIM improved 10 bps to 3.05%, Q4 NIM at 3.07%
items.quote: Last year total cumulative, last entire financial year NIM was 2.95 as against that cur rent year NIM cumulative is at 3.05% with an incremental improvement of 10 basis points

items.statement: Q4 yield on advances rose 11 bps QoQ vs 8 bps rise in incremental interest expenses
items.quote: in the last fourth q uarter, our quarter -on-quarter, incremental growth in the yield on advances were 11 basis points versus the increase in the incremental interest expenses is 8 basis points

items.statement: Reduced low-yield corporate exposure by Rs 10,000-13,000 crore in Q4 from Rs 60,000-70,000 crore pool
items.quote: We reduced such exposure to some extent, around 10,000 to 13,000 crores that has helped us in improving our NIM and the yield on advances.

items.statement: New sanctions higher than last year; credit demand strong in RAM and corporate segments
items.quote: For all practical purposes, for the new sanctions and all, compared to last year, this year new sanctions are much more than what the last year sanctions. So growth will be there, demand is there.

items.statement: RAM advances grew 13.52% YoY to Rs 5.41 lakh crore led by retail 11.68%, agriculture 18.69%, housing 10.81%, vehicle 14.03%
items.quote: 11.34% growth of advances that we announced, is led by our RAM sector grown at 13.52% and stood at Rs. 5, 41, 489 crore out of 9,60,000 crores, and this led by retail credit at 11.68%, agriculture and allied activities have grown at 18.69% and the housing loan has grown at 10.81% and vehicle loan grown at 14.03%.

items.statement: CASA ratio improved 63 bps QoQ to 32.21%; SB individual deposits grew Rs 17,000 crore YoY
items.quote: If you look our fourth quarter CASA, it has improved from 31.65 to 32.21 or something. So that itself is around 63 basis points. It has increased in the fourth quarter because the entire machinery, entire bank, we have focused on CASA.

items.statement: Launched Canara Angel product for women; mobilized Rs 200+ crore in new accounts in first month
items.quote: And already in a one month, we got more than 200 crores deposit mobilization from the new accounts alone, not from the existing accounts.

items.statement: Targeting 33% CASA ratio in FY25; Board strategy aims for 35% in 2 years and 38% in 5 years
items.quote: we are very much confident that in the current year we will achieve that 33% CAS A. And as you said, that it is reaching to 37% to 38%. Definitely it's a long way to go. We are working on

items.quote: Madam, incremental deposit, which is the term deposits, on an ave rage 6.50 to 6.75 is there. But because the CASA is there and the previous outstanding deposits at a lower rate the cost of deposit last compared to quarter is increased from 5.40 to 5.50

items.statement: Corporate loan book yield improved to 8.17% from ~7.05% a year ago (+110 bps)
items.quote: Now it has crossed to 8.05, sir. Earlier it was 7, now it is 8.05... 8.17. 8.17, and we are comfortable with anything above 8%.

items.statement: Credit cost 0.96% (-21 bps YoY), maintained below 1%
items.quote: Our credit cost is again maintained below 1% that stood at 0.96% wit h a year-on-year improvement of 21 basis points

items.statement: Restructured book down to Rs 17,000 crore from Rs 24,000 crore; Rs 12,000 crore standard, Rs 4,800 crore slipped to NPA
items.quote: Total of restructure has made. During that time it was Rs. 24,000 crores. But now as on date outstanding is only Rs. 17,000 crores. Out of that already, Rs. 12,000 crores is standard asset and Rs. 4,800 crores slipped to NPA.

items.statement: Q4 interest on NPA recovery ~Rs 200-250 crore per quarter on average
items.quote: On an average, generally, interest on NPA will come around 200 to 250 crores; that will come in that.

items.statement: IT investment continues; GenAI initiatives planned for customer service, call centre, cyber security
items.quote: Now in the current year, we have targeted for GenAI, artificial intelligence, sir. items.statement: Proposed dividend 161% of paid-up capital vs 120% last year; tempo to continue
items.quote: With this, the Board has permitted us to propose a dividend of 161% of paid up capital as against last year dividend of 120%.

items.statement: Two subsidiary IPOs in advanced stage; one expected Q4 FY25, other Q1 FY26
items.quote: One is in advanced stage, one is still half way. And we expect that one may come to the listing in the last quarter of this financial year. The other one may come in the first quarter of the next financial year.

items.statement: RBI draft project finance circular premature; clarity needed on floor limit; well prepared to absorb impact
items.quote: RBI draft guidelines is still at a premature stage. It was provided only two-three days back. Preliminary we tried to assess it. But we have several doubts on that the guidelines because the guidelines never spoke about what is the floor limit for that project.

items.statement: New investment accounting rules from April 1 added Rs 1,400 crore to reserves, boosting CET1 by 21 bps
items.quote: on implementation of the new accounting guidelines from 1 st of April, it has added about Rs. 1400 crores to our reserves. So that is a positive point which has happened by implementation of

items.quote: The MCLR book is around 51 point odd, that is approximately 52%., sir. Our RLLR linked is 38%. The remaining 10% is staff loans and loans against deposit and all those specific schemes.

items.statement: Investment portfolio yield improved to 6.91% from 6.69% YoY; HTM >80% of portfolio
items.quote: our portfolio yield has increased from 6.69% to 6.91% for the total inv estment portfolio. So, our treasury, our investment portfolio is doing satisfactorily, I can

items.quote: But ultimately our staff cost will stabilize around 4,100. Though it is currently at 4,458 but next quarter onwards our quarterly expenditure what we are looking at is 4,000 to 4,100.

items.statement: Targeting cost-to-income ratio around 47% or lower
items.quote: We are sure that we will maintain CI ratio around 47%. Whatever we could achieve, the cost to income ratio, we will try to maintain that or little to the lower side at 47%.

items.statement: FY25 revenue growth guidance of 7-8% inclusive of Dextara acquisition, with organic growth ~3-4% and inorganic ~4%
items.quote: We expect a growth of 7% to 8%, while maintaining the current margins for the next financial year.

items.statement: FY25 EBITDA margin guidance maintained at 15.7-16% and EBIT margin at 13.5-14%
items.quote: What we are trying to say is basically, we will maintain same kind of margin for next year as well, which is about 15.7% or 16% on EBITDA and 13.5% to 14% on EBIT.

items.statement: Acquired remaining 23% stake in Salesforce-focused JV to consolidate under Dextara
items.quote: We had a small joint venture, which was focused on Salesforce. But after we acquired Dextara, we felt we did not need another entity also focusing on Salesforce. We acquired that, and we will roll this piece of business into the Dextara business.

items.statement: Digital Technologies EBIT margin dropped to 0.7% in Q4 FY24 due to accelerated AI investments and leadership transition costs
items.quote: The investments were ongoing, but we stepped up, we fast tracked a lot of the investments because the space of AI is moving very, very fast. And we needed to make sure that we are in sync with the market. So we did build a lot of these models much faster th an we had originally anticipated. So the expense actually increased

items.statement: Digital Operations EBIT margin spiked to 23.5% in Q4 FY24 due to seasonal pattern and automation implementation
items.quote: So what does happen in Datamatics, in particular, is the Digital Operations piece tends to have a spike in quarter 4. And some of the expenses of that come in quarter 3. So for Q3 tends to be a little softer. Q4 always tends to spike.

items.statement: Digital Experiences EBIT margin at 11.8% in Q4 FY24 after eliminating loss-making projects
items.quote: Our Digital Experiences margin has taken a hit during the year. However, we have eliminated the loss-making projects. Therefore, we will see an improvement in margins through the course of the next financial year.

items.statement: AI investments include small language models, copilots, GenAI integration in TruBot/TruCap+ products rolled out to 30+ customers
items.quote: We have built our own customizable, small language model and copilot and we will be showcasing these capabilities at various industry e vents in the coming year. We have also built an AI framework for our digital experiences business. Through the financial year, we have executed 10 projects in AI. Furthermore, we have incorporated GenAI in our intelligent automation suite of products and have roll

items.statement: Pipeline slowed from INR 245M to INR 200M; Western markets slowing on tech/outsourcing spend
items.quote: The pipeline is slowing down. And right now, it stands at about INR 200 million, and we can see that slowdown happening. And that's why we've been also a little soft on our projections for growth next year.

items.statement: BFSI and Technology verticals expected to remain muted in H1 FY25
items.quote: I think it will remain muted. I don't see any particular vertical picking up right now.

items.statement: Blended utilization 90-95%; onsite ~99%; bench primarily offshore; IP investment not captured in utilization
items.quote: I would imagine that our utilization is in the range of 90% to 95%. We don't carry a very heavy bench. But as you know, we are investing in building some of these IPs and products. So that's where the utilization rate does not fully fit because you're investing in building IP. And that does not go on the utilization rate.

items.statement: Zero debt; cash and investments INR 653 crores as of March 31, 2024
items.quote: We continue to maintain a healthy balance sheet. As of March 31, 2024, our total cash and investment, we have zero debt, it stood at INR 653 crores.

items.statement: Recommended total dividend of INR 5 per share (100% of face value) for FY24
items.quote: I'm happy to share that we have recommended a total dividend of INR 5 per share, that is 100% of the face value of INR 5 each for the year ended March 2024.

items.statement: US 54% of revenue, UK/Europe 13%, Rest of World including India 33%
items.quote: In terms of geographical footprint, US remains our largest geo, with 54% of our business coming from US market, followed by U.K. and Europe at 13% and the rest of the world, including India at 33%.

items.statement: Digital Operations revenue INR 694.4 crores (10.1% YoY), EBIT margin 19.9% for FY24
items.quote: Our Digital Operations revenue was INR694.4 crores, which is 10.1% up from previous year. Digital Operations EBIT margin remains healthy at 19.9%.

items.statement: Digital Experience revenue INR 244 crores (11.2% YoY), EBIT margin 17.1% for FY24
items.quote: Our Digital Experience revenue was to INR 244 crores, which is 11.2% growth over previous year. And Digital Experience EBIT margin remains at 17.1% on a full year basis.

items.statement: Digital Technologies revenue INR 611.5 crores (0.4% YoY), EBIT margin 4.6% for FY24
items.quote: Our Digital Technologies revenue was at INR 611.5 crores, which is slight up 0.4%. EBIT margin for Technology business was at 4.6%.

items.statement: Macro uncertainty causing slowdown in Western tech/outsourcing spend; pipeline softness in Digital Technologies
items.quote: We see the Western world slowing down on their technology and outsourcing spends due to the uncertain macroeconomic environment. However, we expect a growth of 7% to 8%, while maintaining the current margins for the next financial year.

items.statement: AFC business targeting US metro/road deals ($10-40M range); bidding for Pune Metro, evaluating Mumbai Metro lines 4,5,6,9
items.quote: We're targeting the metro and the roads. And road means buses and things like that. And in the metros, there are multiple segments. The top ones like you have Chicago or New York City, these are very large, they are $500 million-plus deals. We will not qualify for those deals. Then the multitude of these that are between $10 million to $40 million. Datamatics qualifies for those deals very well.

items.statement: FY25 EXM payroll growth guided at 20-25% YoY; CXM full-year growth expected in high teens or early 20% range
items.value: 20-25% EXM, high teens to early 20% CXM
items.quote: Coming to EXM, as I have said in the previous calls also, we continue to believe that we can definitely grow in excess of 20% year-on-year. So, I would say that I would put a range of between 20% and 25% in terms of where we would grow the standalone payroll business.

items.statement: FY25 overall revenue growth guided at 18-22% for EXM and similar for CXM; EBITDA margin to see small uptick after investments and inflation
items.quote: So, yes, I think growth and margins have already covered both in the opening remarks and in the answer to the earlier question that we believe that we should be able to grow the respective businesses anywhere between 18% and 22-25% depending, of course, largely in terms of how the new sales span out.

items.statement: FY24 EBITDA margin expanded 200 bps to 24.6%; Q4 CXM segment margin up 77.2% YoY, EXM segment margin up 47.7% YoY
items.quote: EBITDA for the Financial Year is INR 116 crores, a growth of 30.7% from last year. The EBITDA margin increased by 200 bps on a Y-o-Y and FY '24 EBITDA margin stands at 24.6%.

items.statement: EXM Q4 segment margin of 38% includes 3.5% one-time tax vouching benefit; steady-state target ~35%
items.quote: As far as EBITDA margins are concerned, I would just like to point out that the 38% margins have about 3.5% for the one time activities which we do in Q4 on the tax vouching. So, if we adjust this 3.5%, the quarter-on-quarter is about a percent more. The long-term target is around 35%-mark steady state.

items.statement: FY24 EXM new sales ACV INR 27 cr, up 35% YoY; Q4 EXM new sales ACV INR 7 cr vs INR 4 cr in Q3
items.quote: We have signed EXM sales with ACV of 7 crores in Q4, up from INR 4 crores in Q3. For FY '24. We have achieved new sales of ACV INR 27 crores, 35% higher than the previous year.

items.statement: CXM added two new logos aggregating just under INR 100 cr ACV for the year; healthcare account LOBs expanded
items.quote: In CXM we have added new LOBs in the healthcare account which we had won in the end of the previous financial year and also added two new logos aggregating to just under 100 crores ACV for the year.

items.statement: Demand environment stable; corporates open to outsourcing payroll/HR value chain; RFPs continue from in-house payroll
items.quote: We don't see either improvement or a diminution in the demand environment. What we continue to see is that corporates are pretty open to doing payroll or other parts of the HR value chain outsourcing.

items.statement: Manila CXM capacity near full; evaluating cost-effective expansion options; domestic CXM capacity adequate
items.quote: We are pretty much now with near full capacity in Manila. So, for our growth, we will have to keep our options open in terms of whether there are more cost effective options in Manila or we continue to grow in Central Manila where we are currently located.

items.statement: International revenue share rising: CXM international up 39% YoY and 13.3% QoQ; FY24 international contribution increased 12% YoY for EXM
items.quote: FY '24, our overall split between domestic and international was in the region of about 57-43 so 57% from international customers and 43% from domestic customers

items.statement: Q4 collections INR 131.4 cr, up INR 7.1 cr QoQ; cash position robust
items.quote: Our collections for Quarter 4 increased to 131.4 crores up by 7.1 crores quarter-on-quarter.

items.statement: Board recommended final dividend INR 22.9 cr (INR 15/share); FY24 total dividend INR 68.6 cr (INR 45/share), 2.25x prior year
items.quote: Further, the Board of Directors have recommended a final dividend of Rs. 22.9 crores at the rate of Rs. 15 per share, subject to shareholder approval at the ensuing AGM, which brings the total dividend payout for the full year at Rs. 68.6 crores, which would be Rs. 45 a share, 2.25 X (times) of the previous year.

items.statement: Platform upgrade costs (Smart Pay SP4, HRMS v2) already capitalized; no significant incremental capex expected in FY25
items.quote: On your question on platforms, as mentioned in one of our earlier calls, the cost relating to those are already in the balance sheet and those will be amortized over an appropriate period of time, again, as per the market practice and accounting standards.
