items.statement: Average headcount grew ~12% YoY FY23-FY24; March-end headcount just under 6,000; headcount growth to remain in similar ballpark FY25
items.quote: So, the average headcount between FY '23 and FY '24 has grown by about 12%.

items.statement: EXM processes 1.32 million employee records (market leader, 20-30% above competitors); payslips per FTE improved 10% YoY
items.quote: We have added new employee records in excess of 4 lakhs in H2 and now process 1.32 million employee records at the end of March, remaining the clear market leader in the managed services space, being 20% to 30% higher than competitors' volume.

items.statement: CXM FTE grew 9.5% YoY, 1.7% QoQ; attrition maintained at 7.2% per month (near best-in-class)
items.quote: Our staff attrition was maintained at 7.2% per month for Q4, which continues to be near best-in-class in the domestic outsourcing industry.

items.statement: Margin expansion driven by higher international mix, productivity (payslips/FTE), new logos, cost savings; absorbed salary and non-wage inflation
items.quote: A higher share of international and cost savings from operational efficiencies have enabled us to improve EBITDA margins by 200 basis points over FY '23 even after absorbing salary and other inflation.

items.statement: Evaluating niche capability acquisitions in healthcare/RCM; some targets acquired by others at higher valuations; organic build also an option but slower
items.quote: we continue to look at it, I mean, we will continue to balance the niche capability acquisition, the referenceability, the mar ket endorsement which an acquisition can get vis-a-vis what we have to pay for that acquisition. So, we were looking at some assets which have got concluded with other players at a much higher number, then what we were talking about

items.statement: CXM new US sales (hired sales leader March 1, account-based marketing for SME BFSI/Healthcare) expected to contribute only from Q2 FY25; quarterly mining visibility limited
items.quote: We believe that some of the revenues for the new business should only start getting in from Q2 and not prior to that as per our Annual plan.

items.statement: Local Level Compliance (LLC) business sold to Aparajitha Corporate Services; financial closure 30 April 2024; assets classified as held for sale
items.quote: And as far as the held for proceed (held for sale) number is concerned, that relates to our LLC transaction, which was the sale of our local level compliance business to Aparajitha C orporate Services. The formal financial closure of the transaction happened only on 30th April

items.statement: Management expects ~10% volume growth in coming years and targets value-added product mix >50% of revenue within 1-1.5 years
items.quote: So considering everything put together, we should be in a range of volumes. We should consider 10% around volumes for the coming up, coming years.

items.statement: Debt repayment of INR145 cr in FY25 and INR174 cr in FY26; no new loans planned for FY25
items.quote: Secondly, as far as going forward we are definitely tearing down some of our debt which is a normal repayment of debt of about INR150 crores in the next year. So that will definitely come down.

items.statement: Routine capex INR15-20 cr/year; major expansion capex not yet decided; INR840 cr invested over last 1.5 years (30% to fabric/knitting, rest to spinning)
items.value: INR15-20 cr routine; major capex TBD
items.quote: Normal capex, which is of the routine nature, is about INR15 crores to INR20 crores t hat is happening. That happens every year due to various requirements for debottlenecking and other things. Apart from that, major capex plan has not yet been decided

items.statement: Yarn capacity ~91k tons vs rated 110k tons (max 105k tons); fabric/weaving can improve 7-8%; knitting utilization lower with scope to improve; overall ~10% volume headroom
items.quote: Our rated capacity is around 1,10,000 tons per annum. And we can produce, after giving all efficiencies and others, about 1,05,000 tons. So, we are looking for that kind of capacity utilization which is about 10% more from the present last year's capacity.

items.statement: Q4 FY24 EBITDA margin 14.52%; management indicates maintaining ~14.5% would be substantial improvement over FY24 average 13%; long-term target 16-20% if export demand and FTAs materialize
items.quote: Basically, we do not give any projections for the margins. But just an indication is that our last quarter margin was 14.5. So, if you are able to maintain that also it should be substantial improvement from the existing levels, yearly levels.

items.statement: Cotton prices stable at INR57-58k/candy (±INR3k) for 6-8 months; expected to remain stable this calendar year; yarn realization FY24 INR274/kg vs FY23 INR338/kg (-19%); fabric realization FY24 INR160/m vs FY23 INR182/m
items.quote: Cotton prices have remained in the range of INR 57,000, INR58,000 plus minus INR3,000 a candy for good last 6 months, 7 months, 8 months which is going to continue going forward as well as we look forward.

items.statement: Export demand improving at normal pace; China re-importing cotton yarn (+35-40% YoY in March); Indian exports improved last 6-8 months, expected stable next 6 months; full demand recovery may take 5-6 more months
items.quote: Demand is definitely improving and it is not a very fast pace. It is a normal pace. If you see the data of imports by various of these countries we are seeing that China has started to re-import large quantities.

items.statement: Export mix targeted at 55-60% of revenue (down from 73% in FY22); domestic and export realizations similar; exports include both yarn and fabric
items.quote: As a strateg y, we would rather keep ourselves limited up to 50 -- in the band of 55 % to 60% on the export side. And that's what we're doing

items.statement: Total debt INR1,339 cr (INR811 cr long-term, INR383 cr WC, INR145 cr current maturities); term debt 5.5% net of subsidies (new loans at full rate pending sanction); WC ~7.5%; debt/equity 1.15-1.16; target interest cost 2.5-3% of revenue
items.quote: As of March 24, the company's debt profile stood at INR1,339 crores comprising INR811 crores in long-term debt, INR383 crores working capital and INR145 crores as current maturities of term loan.

items.statement: Solar capacity increased from 12-13 MW to 23 MW (+10 MW); adding 7-8 MW more in current year; solar generation ~2.7 cr units/yr at lower cost vs grid INR7-7.5/unit; renewables 7-8% of power mix; INR95-100 cr invested in solar over 3 years
items.quote: We have added substantial solar capacity -- solar power capacity. Now our capacity is about 23 megawatts. If you see at the end of the last year this capacity was about 12, 13 megawatts. So we have added more than 10 megawatts of capacity.

items.statement: Value-added products ~38-40% of revenue (fabric 25-26% + value-added yarn 14-15%); target >50% in 1-1.5 years
items.quote: So that all put together, it is about 38 % to 40%, where we do a reasonable value addition in comparison to normal commodity yarns. So this proportion slowly is going up. We expect that total, we should be doing it more than 50%.

items.statement: Government schemes (textile parks, PLI, export incentives) delayed due to elections; expected implementation post-elections to aid long-term growth; FTA with EU could benefit >20% of sales (UK only 3-4%)
items.quote: The measures were in active consideration, however held up due to elections. I hope implementation of these schemes post -elections will h elp long-term growth of Indian textile industry

items.statement: Board recommended dividend 25% (INR2.5/share), same as last year
items.quote: The Board of Directors has recommended a dividend of 25% i.e. INR2.5 per share, i.e. same as last year.

items.statement: Captive consumption 20% of yarn production; depreciation run-rate INR36 cr/quarter (INR145 cr/yr) on current asset base
items.quote: Yeah, this INR36 crores every quarter will be charged. So the average -- the depreciation next year is expected to be on the current set of fixed assets is about INR145 crores.

items.statement: Geopolitical risks (Russia-Ukraine, Red Sea crisis) increasing freight costs and transit times; margin recovery dependent on export demand pickup and FTA implementation
items.quote: Despite ongoing geopolitical challenges such as Russia-Ukraine conflict, Red Sea crisis, which has resulted in a higher freight cost and extended transit times, our country's cotton textile exports have demonstrated a healthy rebound.

items.statement: Target to double AUM to $125 billion by 2030; could reach by 2029 if 15-20% growth sustained
items.quote: REC management and board have decided to have a clear-cut roadmap and we are targeting to double our asset under management to about $125 billion by the year 2030.

items.statement: Target renewable energy portfolio to grow 10x to $40 billion by 2030 from current $4 billion
items.quote: We are trying to increase our renewable energy portfolio by 10x to about $40 billion by the end 2030.

items.statement: Target non-power infrastructure logistics AUM to grow fourfold to $25 billion by 2030
items.quote: We are anticipating that our total asset under management from non-power infrastructure logistics will see fourfold growth to say about $25 billion by the end of 2030.

items.statement: Expect 30% AUM from renewables, 15-20% from non-power infra, 50-55% from conventional by 2030
items.quote: By the year 2030, we would like to double our asset under management to about $125 billion, 30% of it will come from renewable energy segment, 15% to 20% will come from non-power infrastructure logistics, and 50% to 55% of asset under management will come from conventional coal-based generation capacity, distribution and transmission sector.

items.statement: Sanctioned projects worth $43 billion in FY24, up 34% from $32.2 billion in FY23
items.quote: We sanctioned projects worth $43 billion in the last financial year, as compared to $32.2 billion which we had sanctioned in FY23.

items.statement: Disbursements grew 67% to $19.3 billion in FY24 from $11.6 billion in FY23
items.quote: The disbursements have also grown by 67% or total disbursement stood around $19.3 billion last financial year, as compared to $11.6 billion in FY23.

items.statement: Renewable energy sanctions pipeline of over INR175,000 crores for current financial year
items.quote: In the current financial year, we have a huge pipeline of projects amounted to more than INR175,000 crores.

items.statement: Cost of funds reduced 15 bps to 7.13% in FY24; spread improved 41 bps to 2.86%; NIM up 19 bps to 3.57%
items.quote: We were able to bring down our cost of funds by 15 bps from 7.28% in the last financial year to 7.13% in FY '24. The spread has already improved by 41 basis points from 2.45% to 2.86%. The net interest margin has seen an increase of 19 bps from 3.38% to 3.57%.

items.statement: Profit after tax grew 29% to $2.12 billion (PBT); net profit up 27% to $1.68 billion in FY24
items.quote: Our total profit after tax at the end of the financial year was about $2.12 billion -- profit before tax, sorry, profit before tax. And our net profit has seen an increase of 27%. It was about $1.68 billion.

items.statement: Return on net worth at 22.17% in FY24
items.quote: Our return on net worth was about 22.17%.

items.statement: Power demand increased 8% in FY24 and 11% in April 2024
items.quote: Last year, power demand increased by 8%. And in the current financial in the last month in April, power demand has increased by 11%.

items.statement: RBI draft circular proposes phased additional provisioning for under-construction projects: 2% by Mar-25, 3.5% by Mar-26, 5% by Mar-27
items.quote: But it's to be effected in phased manner by 31st March, 2025, only 2% provision has to be done. By 31st March 2026, 3.5% provisioning has to be done. And by 31st March, 2027, 5% crossing has to be done.

items.statement: RBI draft guidelines not applicable to loans backed by state government guarantees (~40% of loan book)
items.quote: This RBI guideline would not be applicable to these loans which have been supported by the state government guarantee. About 40% of our loan is supported by the state government guarantee.

items.statement: Distribution CapEx loans backed by state guarantees (65% of distribution portfolio) exempt from RBI provisioning
items.quote: the total book size under the distribution segment is close to 25.75 billion, out of which the CapEx which is supposed to attract provisioning requirement is only 9 billion, which is just 35% of total dis tribution portfolio

items.statement: Expect write-backs of INR1,500-2,000 crores in FY25; target net zero NPA by end FY25
items.quote: We are expecting a write-back to the tune of INR1,500 crores to INR2,000 crores in the financial year FY '25. And we hope that all this asset would get resolved in the current financial year itself and will become net zero NPA company by the end of FY '25.

items.statement: Gross NPA INR13,800 crores; INR2,222 crores (7 projects) fully provided heading to liquidation
items.quote: Our gross NPA is about INR13,800 crores. And out of that, about 7 projects are heading towards liquidation that is amounting to INR2,222 crores. For this, we already made 100% provisioning.

items.statement: Capital adequacy ratio 25.82% vs 15% minimum; Tier 1 capital 23.32% vs 10% minimum
items.quote: Our minimum capital ratio required is 15%, and we are having about 25.82%. For Tier 1 capital, the RBI statutory minimum requirement is 10%, and we are having to the tune of 23.32%.

items.statement: May pass on some RBI provisioning impact to borrowers via higher lending rates, but lower borrowing costs may offset
items.quote: We'll have to pass on some impact of this -- we'll be able to pass on to the borrower. But another -- the silver line of fact is that, our cost of borrowing is going to come down in after Q2, Q3. Once this cost of borrowing comes down, we'll pass on or perhaps balance out actually.

items.statement: Green bond funding provides 10-15 bps cost advantage for renewable projects, offsetting provisioning impact
items.quote: There are a number of lenders who are willing to lend at slightly lower rates as compared to the normal raising, which we are doing, both in domestic market as well as the international market. So there are enough funds which are available, and the differential is about 10 to 15 basis points as compared to the normal borrowing which we are doing for general purposes, for conventional generation al

items.statement: Additional 94 GW coal capacity identified by 2032; REC targets 30-40% share of capex financing
items.quote: About 94 gigawatt capacity has been identified to be brought in by year 2032, in the next 8 years, all the approvals for this additional coal-based capacity will happen next 2 to 3 years. There also, we see a huge potential or REC, we'll be able to share at 30% to 40% of the coal base capacity, addition capital would be coming in the next 8 years.

items.statement: Distribution infrastructure upgrade opportunity over next 10-12 years as assets are 40-50 years old
items.quote: After RDSS period is over and the modernization is over, in the next 4 to 5 years, country will still require a lot of CapEx for upgrading the infrastructure, because distribution infrastructure all the poles, wires, the distribution transformer is quite old, 40 to 50 years old.

items.statement: Renewable sanctions in FY24: large hydro INR32,450 Cr, pump storage INR28,304 Cr, solar INR21,000 Cr, module manufacturing INR21,565 Cr, green hydrogen INR8,000 Cr, e-mobility INR8,000 Cr
items.quote: Last year, we sanctioned project of INR136,515 crores. Out of this, large hydro projects constitute about INR32,450 crores, pump storage hydro project was about INR28,304 crores; followed by solar, about INR21,000 crores. Then model manufacturing was INR21,565 crores; followed by green hydrogen project, about INR8,000 crores we have sanctioned; electric mobility, about INR8,000 crores.

items.statement: RBI draft guidelines may reduce Tier 1 capital by INR2,000-3,000 crores over 3 years but won't impact approval process
items.quote: Even if this Tier 1 capital gets reduced by say 2,000 to 3,000, it will not impact our approval process.

items.statement: Only ~20% of AUM (INR1 lakh crore) impacted by RBI draft guidelines; 80% of renewable book already commissioned
items.quote: Out of 5 lakh crores this asset under management, most of them are already commissioned. Only 1 lakh crore of projects are under construction, which will get impacted.

items.statement: Ramped up manpower and hired sector experts for infrastructure logistics appraisal since Oct 2022 diversification
items.quote: We have ramped up our manpower strength. We have got in experts from different fields, putting to infrastructure logistics.

items.statement: Government committed to 50 GW annual renewable capacity addition from FY25 vs 12-14 GW previously
items.quote: From this year onwards, they stepped up their ambitions and per annum, they are targeting installation of 50 gigawatt capacities.

items.statement: RBI draft guidelines on project finance exposure norms will impact Tier 1 capital; state government guaranteed loans are kept out of exposure norms per common understanding with RBI.
items.quote: As for exposure is concerned, we are very clear that state government guaranteed loan are not counted. Yes, out of the purview.

items.statement: RBI draft guidelines apply to all under-construction capex projects regardless of DCCO extension; company will request RBI to limit applicability to DCCO-funded projects only.
items.quote: It will be on all under-construction project -- all CapEx projects. So we have made it clear, it will be affecting all the under construction projects despite whether it is DCCO shift or not.

items.statement: Loan book grew 17% in current year; if sustained, INR 10 lakh crore target could be reached by FY29 instead of FY30.
items.quote: If we are able -- like this year, our asset grew by about 17%. If this 17% growth is continued, then we'll be able to reach this INR10 lakh crores by the year 2029 itself, in next 5 years, not 6 years.

items.statement: Targeting minimum INR 175,000 crore disbursements this year, up from INR 151,000 crore last year, with significant increase in capex disbursements.
items.quote: But this year, o ur CapEx disbursement are going to jump quite substantially. And we are targeting minimum INR175,000 crores

items.statement: Renewable energy share of total assets to grow from 7% to 30% in 5-6 years; conventional generation 29% growing 2-3% annually; distribution & transmission 40% stable; logistics 15-20% by 2030.
items.quote: Right now, share of renewable energy is only 7% of our total assets. It will gradually increase to 30% in the next 5 to 6 years. So every year, we see that incremental growth of 5% to 7% growth will be there as far as renewable energy is concerned.

items.statement: Spread expected to improve from 2.8% to 3% driven by higher-margin coal-based generation (94 GW pipeline, 40% share target), large hydro, pump storage, and non-power infra.
items.quote: So we do hope that our spread is going to improve further, not going to come down. It may go up to 3% actually, from 2.8% it may increase to 3% actually.

items.statement: Cost of funds reduced 15 bps from 7.28% to 7.13%; ECB share increased from 24% to 29%; all-in ECB cost 6.6-6.7% via innovative hedging; 54EC bonds target >INR 50,000 crore.
items.quote: You might have seen that our cost of funds has come down by 15 basis points from 7.28% to 7.13%. And the share of our external commercial borrowing has increased from 24% to 29%.

items.statement: 7 projects worth INR 2,222 crore heading for liquidation, fully provisioned; no new NPA added in last 9 quarters; targeting net NPA zero by FY25.
items.quote: Not 9, 7 projects are getting towards liquidation, total value of INR2,222 crores, for which we already made 100% provisioning.

items.statement: No impairment reserve currently as Ind AS provisioning already exceeds IRAC norms; standard asset provisioning ~0.5% overall, up to 1% on individual projects.
items.quote: Our provisioning is already higher than the IRAC norms, there is no impairment reserves at present.

items.statement: Power demand grew 8% last year and 11% in April; DISCOM AT&C losses fell from 22% to 15.5% over 2 years under RDSS; state gencos/transcos health improving.
items.quote: The AT&C loss, which was 22% 2 years back, came down to roughly 16.5% and then it has now further come down to 15.5%.

items.statement: 94 GW coal-based capacity pipeline; targeting minimum 40% business share; lending rates 10-11% for coal projects with ability to pass on incremental provisioning costs.
items.quote: You might have observed that our lending rate is the highest in respect of coal based capacity only. It varies from 10% to 11% actually. This 94 gigawatt capacity, some additional impact was because additional provisioning some impact would be there, that we'll be able to pass on actually.

items.statement: RBI draft guidelines may impair bank lending capacity for private capex, creating opportunity for REC to capture high-quality assets with less competition.
items.quote: But then that gives us greater opportunity. In any case, we are a very active lender in the power sector space, and we started lending operations in the interest space as well.

items.statement: Tier 1 capital impact from RBI guidelines to be calculated after final norms; comments due by June; impact may reflect in Q1 or Q2 results depending on final guideline timing.
items.quote: So whatever impact will be there in any case, the comments are to be sent by June. So in case they come out with the final guidelines before the first quarterly results, then in any case, we'll be having the impact there in the first quarterly result itself.

items.statement: Collections increasing; 54EC capital gains tax saving bonds at INR 40,000 crore targeting >INR 50,000 crore; foreign currency borrowing with innovative hedging at 6.6-6.7% all-in cost.
items.quote: One is 54 EC bonds that is capital gains tax saving ins trument, that is about 40,000. That also will increase to more than INR50,000 crores. That's what we are targeting.Collections are going to increase

items.statement: Bridge financing and RBPF not covered under RBI project finance definition as DCCO required; only projects meeting specific definition fall under new norms.
items.quote: There is a definition of project which is given under these guidelines. So we have to go by that definition. So these type of bridge financing which they are doing or even if we are doing RBPF for this type of funding, so that won't be covered in -- because in any case, DCCO has to be there for these type of project.

items.statement: Banks largely absent from infra financing; private sector banks (ICICI, HDFC) not in infra; state banks lend to REC which on-lends to projects leveraging REC's evaluation capability.
items.quote: Actually, banks in any case are not lending for the infra. In case you see the private sector banks, ICICI, HDFC nowhere they are in case of the infra financing. It's only the state sector banks which are there.

items.statement: 70% of profits retained to grow net worth (ROE >20%), 30% paid as dividend; write-backs from stressed asset resolutions (KSK etc.) expected next year.
items.quote: So there'll be 70% in any case will be going towards the net worth itself, 30% we have to declare by way of dividend. Remaining will be incrementally going towards the net worth itself.

items.statement: No management changes or key hires mentioned in transcript.
items.quote: On behalf of REC, I would like to thank all the participants for asking inquisitive questions and hope that we have been able to answer your queries and on the various issues to your satisfaction.

items.statement: FY25 revenue expected around INR 5,500-5,600 crore based on order book execution
items.quote: So, INR 1,700 crores of CV, about INR 3,600 crores of wagon. So that means INR 5,300 crores and maybe some amount of the current year order book executed. So, about INR 5,500 crores, INR 5,600 crores turnover is a reasonable possibility, right? For the current year?

items.statement: Order backlog at INR 7,10,166 lakh, highest ever, with 75% wagons executable over 18 months and balance CV business in FY25
items.quote: In terms of outlook, we are pleased to report an order backlog of INR 7,10,166 lakh our highest ever.

items.statement: Capex of INR 1,000-1,500 crore planned for Bonatrans wheel set backward integration over 18-24 months
items.quote: In terms of investments, I think our Capex in this business will be anything between INR1,000 crores to INR1,500 crores of Capex, which we are looking to invest in this business.

items.statement: Targeting 1,000 wagons/month run rate by Q2 FY25; Bonatrans wheel set capacity to expand from 15,000-20,000 to 100,000 sets/annum
items.quote: By I think quarter 2 is what we are looking at.

items.statement: Visible margin improvement expected in FY25 from wheel sets, brakes, and specialized wagons; brake business margins upward of 14-15%
items.quote: It will not be something marginal, but there'll be a visible improvement in margins.

items.statement: Shift to specialized wagons (steel, cement, auto), BESS/data center containers, and brake systems driving higher margins
items.quote: We are now working with a lot of marquee names global names, such as GE, Schneider, Toshiba, Tata Solar.

items.statement: Private wagon market share 60-70%; order wins from Ministry of Railways, Ministry of Defence, and leading auto manufacturer
items.quote: Jupiter continues to dominate the private segment. So if you look at the private order books, I think Jupiter share would be more than 60% to 70% in this segment.

items.statement: Acquired Bonatrans India for wheel set manufacturing; Stone India integration on track
items.quote: During the quarter, we acquired Bonatrans India Private Limited which further solidifies our integrated business model.

items.statement: Rail freight modal mix projected to rise from 29% (FY24) to 35% by FY31
items.quote: Projections indicate a rise in the rail freight modal mix from 29% in fiscal year 2024 to 35% by fiscal year 2031.

items.statement: Net debt near zero after QIP; long-term borrowings nil, sufficient cash available
items.quote: Net debt is around 0 because the long-term borrowing we don't have, and we have the sufficient cash available.

items.statement: Board approved INR 1,000 crore fundraise (mix of equity and debt) primarily for wheel business capex
items.quote: The Board, I think, has cleared fresh set of, I think, INR 1,000 crores of new capital fundraise the Board has cleared. So it will be a mix of both debt as well as equity.

items.statement: Bonatrans FY25 revenue target INR 300-400 crore (captive + external); 14,000-18,000 wheel sets production
items.quote: This year, we are looking to produce about close to 14,000-to-18,000-wheel sets in Bonatrans and we are looking at revenues of about INR400-odd crores.

items.statement: Brake systems (KOVIS/DAKO) FY25 revenue at least INR 300 crore combined
items.quote: We are looking at least about INR 300 crores of revenue at least in both the businesses.

items.statement: eLCV launch expected July 2024; FY25 target upward of 500 vehicles, margin positive from day 1
items.quote: We are expecting the approval to come any day, I think, in the next week or 10 days, I think we expect approvals to be there. And I've maintained that July, we are going to be launching a vehicle.

items.statement: Greenfield foundry in Jabalpur ~INR 200 crore for weldable crossings; 18-month timeline
items.quote: About close to INR 200 crores, if I am not wrong for...

items.statement: Weldable crossing market size INR 4,000-5,000 crore; railway to buy >100,000 crossings in 3-4 years
items.quote: So, it is about -- the market is about INR 4,000 crores to INR 5,000 crores is the market size.

items.statement: Working capital ~75 days in FY24, expected to remain same in FY25; debtor days stable at 49 days
items.quote: The working capital is around 75 days. And I think that will remain in FY '25 also.

items.statement: Final dividend INR 0.30/share recommended; combined with interim INR 0.30, total FY24 dividend INR 0.60/share
items.quote: The Board of Directors has recommended a final dividend of INR 0.30 per share, accompanied by the interim dividend of INR 0.30 per share, the combined dividend for financial year 2023-'24 amounts to INR 0.60 per share.

items.statement: Strong private wagon demand continues; BOXN wagon tender hold expected to lift post-elections; railway tender of ~6,000 wagons nearing finalization
items.quote: Already, there is one tender. I don't remember that I think it's close to about 6,000 wagons, which is going to be finalized very shortly.

items.statement: Vande Bharat tenders margin-negative; focusing on component supply (brakes, wheel sets, battery systems) where competition limited
items.quote: But definitely, we are not partnering with them to -- partnering with anybody to bid for the tenders because, again, which we feel that these are very margin negative right now, the pricing is very margin negative.

items.statement: Significant export potential for wheel sets to Tatravagonka (Europe) due to Russia-Ukraine conflict; Bonatrans certified for Europe and North America
items.quote: Further, I think there's a significant export potential because one of our significant partners and promoters in Jupiter Wagon, which is Tatravagonka, they are again, very keen to acquire wheel sets from India.

items.statement: No management changes mentioned; focus on consolidating new segments
items.quote: I think right now, we are looking to consolidate all the new segments which we have entered into.

items.statement: Foundry capacity constraint limiting CMS crossings and weldable crossings; dependent on capacity additions
items.quote: So, a lot of the capacity was towards wagons. And that's why there's a drop in the CMS numbers.

items.statement: eLCV regulatory approval expected within 1-2 weeks; weldable crossing RDSO final approval in couple of months
items.quote: We are expecting the approval to come any day, I think, in the next week or 10 days, I think we expect approvals to be there.

items.statement: Specialized private wagons command better pricing and margins vs railway wagons; passenger wheel sets higher margin than freight
items.quote: Compared to freight per wheel set, both in terms of the pricing and definitely in terms of margins because these are more complicated wheel sets. So it's much better than on the freight business.

items.statement: Backward integration of wheel sets to control quality, timelines, cost; currently buying black materials externally
items.quote: today, we have to buy black materials from outsi de. And then we do the assembly and the machining and everything all those operations are

items.statement: Long-term target: INR 10,000 crore revenue in 3-4 years (wheel sets INR 3,000 cr, brakes INR 1,000 cr)
items.quote: So, Bharat ji, definitely not. As I mentioned that -- on the wheelset, I think all the Capex is done, that is going to be a significant contributor if we produce about 100,000 wheelsets, we are looking at revenues of upwards of INR 3,000 crore there.

items.statement: Management expects 15-20% topline growth in FY25 and PAT growth of around 1% above FY24 levels
items.quote: We are expecting topline growth of around and I am being very conservative, but we are expecting a topline growth of around 15% to 20% and trying to take up the net profit like it went up by about 1%-1.5% this year. So, maybe another one that is a conservative approach

items.statement: Management targets Rs 500 crore topline ASAP
items.quote: we plan to touch Rs. 500 crores of topline ASAP.

items.statement: Cotton seed industry faces supply shortage due to monsoon vagaries and labor shortage; company may not meet full demand
items.quote: we expect shortage of cotton seed in the current year overall for the industry and which will be the same case with us . We may not be able to supply the total qu antity really in demand for Nath Seeds

items.statement: Gross margin exceeded 55% in FY24; maintained 53-55% range over recent years
items.quote: The gross margin also exceeded 55% during the year as compared to earlier years. I would like to reiterate that we have been maintaining a gross margin of around 53%, 54%, 55% over the last few years.

This takes the full-year dividend to INR8.50 per share, almost at the same level as last year.

items.statement: Onboarded VFX Supervisor Dan Levitan with 30+ years experience and 85 feature films, and COO Zameer with 20+ years at ILM, MPC, DNEG

items.statement: Launched upskilling program to convert 2D VFX artists into 3D concept artists with 100% employee participation

items.statement: Expanding project portfolio into emerging markets Italy, Spain, France and seeing surge from North America post writers' strike resolution
items.quote: BFS is expanding its project portfolio with new ventures originating from emerging markets such as Italy, Spain, and France, as well as experiencing assertive projects from the established markets of North America post the resolution of the writers' strike.

items.quote: PLI, so far we have got the cer tiﬁcate for Tiago EV. And right now the SOP for disbursement is being ﬁnalized. And we are hoping that in the second half of this ﬁnancial year, we may start getting the disbursement. We are also going to apply for additi onal two products in Q1 and for the additional one product in Q2 also

items.statement: Management expects FY25 volume growth of around 10% and EBITDA margin of 20-22%
items.quote: we have always been optimistic, and we always feel that 10% to 15% growth rate has been our norm. There have been a few years like last year where we have dropped below that. But otherwise, 10% is, I think, what we expect.

items.statement: FY24 capex was INR120 crores; FY25 capex planned at INR60-80 crores plus potential INR75-200 crores for new products over 2 years
items.quote: this year, our total capital expenditure is about INR120 crores. In that INR120 crores is also some expenditure for routine maintenance capex and the solar plant to supply electricity to our Dahej facility.

items.statement: Ethylamine plant (100 TPD, INR375 cr capitalized) commissioned and running well; utilization ~60% in H2 FY24
items.quote: the ethylamines plant, which we had been constructing over the last 2, 2.5 years has been commissioned and has been running very well much better than our expectations. And it is now probably the largest ethylamine plant in the world.

items.statement: Acetonitrile plant utilization ~55-60% in H2 FY24 due to Chinese competition
items.quote: The second half was not as good as the first half because the Chinese pressure continued in terms of price and aggressive selling in the Indian market. So -- we were at about half our capacity 55%, a little better than half.

items.statement: Pharma demand stable and growing; agrochemical destocking ending but Chinese competition increasing
items.quote: the market demand for pharma is quite stable now and growing. And we have managed to increase our sales in terms of tonnage.

items.statement: Ethylamine margins improved in last 3-4 months due to lower ethanol prices and stable selling prices; methylamine margins stable; MIPA margins pressured after anti-dumping duty expiry
items.quote: But as far as pricing is concerned, yes, it has improved on both the selling side as well as the raw material side, the ethyl alcohol has softened. compared to what it was, say, 6 months, | year ago.

items.statement: EBITDA margin target 20-22%; FY24 average selling price dropped ~20%, top line down ~14%
items.quote: I would say that 20% EBITDA margin is what we hope to achieve between 20% and 22%.

items.statement: FY24 volume growth under 10% (just short of 1 lakh tons); H2 weaker due to acetonitrile and MIPA pressure
items.quote: Yes, total volume growth for the whole year is under 10%. Second half was much -- I mean, it was disappointing largely under pressure from Acetonitrile, as I said earlier, to Nilesh.

items.statement: Acetonitrile prices stabilized around INR145-160/kg; ethylamine prices INR150-160/kg; raw materials: ammonia INR50-52/kg, acetic acid <INR40/kg, methanol <INR30/kg
items.quote: About INR150 or so. For the larger people INR145, for the smaller people INR160 that kind.

items.statement: Chinese competition across products (acetonitrile, MIPA, methylamine); Balaji adding 40k ton methylamine plant; Chinese methylamine capacity announcement noted
items.quote: it's not just acetonitrile, it's across the board, they have too much capacity in most of their chemical industry. And in fact, we recently saw an announcement by one of their companies for a huge methylamines plant.

items.statement: Anti-dumping duty investigation on acetonitrile initiated March 2024; interim relief possible Q4 FY25; injury estimated 15-20%
items.quote: we have filed antidumping in December and in March '24, the investigation has been initiated, hearings are going on right now and we are planning for filing interim relief also in that. But it will take time. Maybe in Q4 of '24-'25, we expect that to come, if it is favorable on our side. Injury is in the range of 15% to 20%.

items.statement: FY24 sales mix: ~40-50% amines, ~25% derivatives, ~20-25% specialty (mainly acetonitrile)
items.quote: It's still, I think, in the region of 40% to 50% is the main Amines about 25% is derivatives and about 20% to 25% is specialty, which is the main one being Acetonitrile.

items.statement: Other expenses up INR15 crores QoQ due to CSR provision, Patalganga asset impairment, higher power/fuel from increased production
items.quote: So mainly CSR expenses, which we could not spend, we had to make provision for that, and there was one asset at Patalganga, which was not being used, so we had to impair that. and since there is increase in production, the power and fuel expenses have increased.

items.statement: Solar capacity 8.5 MW total (3.5 MW added in Jan FY24); saves INR3-4 crores/year vs grid; power cost lower in FY24 due to lower coal prices
items.quote: Yes, about -- my estimate would be these 8 megawatts would be giving you about INR3 crores to INR4 crores of savings in view of if you were buying from the grid, right?

items.statement: Old ethylamine plant at Patalganga (15k tons) to be converted to methylamine over ~2 years; Dahej methylamine plant at 80-85% utilization (45k tons/yr)
items.quote: No, we are having plans to convert it into methylamines. The engineering has just started. It would take a little time to convert it but_we are preparing for 2 years down the line when the demand has grown to a level where we will need it.

items.statement: Acetonitrile market size 30-35k tons; 50-55% imported in FY24
items.quote: Market size would be in the range of 30,000 to 35,000 tons. And I would say about 50% of that estimated is imported last year. 50% to 55% was imported.

items.statement: FY25 pre-sales guidance of Rs.1,350-1,400 crores, implying 33-35% growth over FY24
items.quote: In all of these projects, launches and the expansions, we are looking at a guidance of about 33% to 35% growth in our pre-sales figure from what we did this year, where we are aiming between Rs.1,350 plus crores in this FY25.

items.statement: Target to reduce debt-to-equity ratio to 0.8x by end of FY25
items.quote: And our target is to bring this to 0.8x by the end of this fiscal year.

items.statement: EBITDA margin expected to remain stable at 30% or above in FY25
items.quote: But however, the EBITDA margin should be in the range of 30% or 30% plus kind of a thing, as we are maintaining the stable margin out of the portfolio.

items.statement: Revenue visibility of Rs.6,400 crores from OC received, ongoing projects and launch pipeline over ~4 years
items.quote: With our OC received and ongoing project portfolio, we have a revenue visibility of Rs.1,860 crores from our ongoing projects. And we are expecting Rs.4,570 crores of the launch pipeline. And that is going to deepen further the revenue visibility to totaling to Rs.6,400 crores.

items.statement: Estimated net cash flow of Rs.750 crores from OC received and ongoing portfolio
items.quote: The 5 estimated net cash flow from OC received and ongoing portfolio is estimated to be Rs.750 crores

items.statement: FY24 pre-sales of Rs.1,017 crores and 4.73 lakh sq ft; Q4 FY24 sales of Rs.287 crores and 1.13 lakh sq ft
items.quote: Our sales value and revenue crossed the mark of, in the history, and hence we have achieved the back of pre-sales of Rs.1,017 crores and the pre-sale area of 4,73,000 square feet.

items.statement: Manhattan project 76% sold, Eden project >50% sold in first year, Prive project 38% sold, Bangalore projects 85% sold
items.quote: Our flagship, Ajmera Manhattan Project which is in Wadala has seen about 76% sales already happening in that project. Whereas I am very proud to say we are currently just above the podium parking levels on the E-deck level, and we still have about 35 to 36 floors to complete.

items.statement: Greenfinity next phase launched in Q4 FY24, 19% sold
items.quote: We also launched Greenfinity the next phase during this quarter and have sold about 19% of its inventory, and the project is currently at the exploration stage.

items.statement: Plan to launch 8 projects in FY25 with total GDV of Rs.4,500+ crores and 1.9 million sq ft development
items.quote: We are about to launch about 8 projects with a total GDV of about Rs.4,500 plus crores with a total development of about 1.9 million square feet.

items.statement: New Wadala phase with GDV of Rs.1,500 crores to be launched in FY25
items.quote: I am very happy to say that on the back of a profound sales of Ajmera Manhattan, we are also adding in our existing new launches, a new phase of Wadala, which will have a GDV of about Rs.1,500 crores.

items.statement: Business development pipeline targeting Rs.3,000-3,500 crores of new projects in FY25
items.quote: We also have further guided that we are also looking at our portfolio expansions wherein we are under advanced talks to a lot of projects, and hopefully that should materialize during this financial year, the coming financial year. And we are looking to add about Rs.3,000 crores to Rs.3,500 crores of project in our pipeline from what we are existing already having.

items.statement: Manhattan new phase targeting launch in Q4 FY25
items.quote: Our estimate is that towards the last quarter of FY25 we should be able to launch this.

items.statement: Kanjurmarg project phase launch planned in FY25, Bhandup project official launch by June 2024
items.quote: And definitely we are going to launch one of the phases this financial year. And we are working on the same. And hopefully we should be giving a good announcement soon.

items.statement: Existing land bank of ~12 million sq ft carpet area (Wadala, Kanjurmarg, others) to be launched over next 2-4 years
items.quote: With our existing portfolio and existing land banks, that is Wadala, Kanjurmarg and other places, we have about 12-odd million square feet of carpet area to be launched.

items.statement: FY24 EBITDA margin 30%, PAT margin 15%; Q4 FY24 EBITDA Rs.69 crores, PAT Rs.29 crores
items.quote: EBITDA stood at Rs.209 crores which is 56% Y-o-Y increase, which is having the EBITDA margin of 30%. And PAT stood at Rs.103 crores, witnessing 44% Y-o-Y growth, resulting in a PAT margin of 15%.

items.statement: Manhattan realization increased from Rs.28,500/sq ft (FY23) to Rs.31,100/sq ft (FY24)
items.quote: To give you a very significant sales contribution from the Manhattan, last year FY23, on an average basis Manhattan had a 28,500 plus on a carpet basis, which has moved up to 31,100 on FY24 basis.

items.statement: Redevelopment project margins: slum 18-22%, society 25-35%, MHADA 30-35%, own land 40-50%
items.quote: Whenever it is a slum, it is usually around 18% to 22%. If it is society, it is about 25% to 35%. MHADA redevelopment is about 30%, 35%. So, that's where we range. And if it is our own land, then it is about 40%, 50%.

items.statement: Debt stable at Rs.780 crores, debt-to-equity 0.9x, weighted average cost of debt below 12%
items.quote: I am pleased to inform that despite aggressive business development activities, our debt remained stable at Rs.780 crores, improving the debt equity ratio below 1x benchmark and precisely at 0.9x to equity. The weighted average cost of the debt remains stable and below 12%.

items.statement: FY24 collections Rs.570 crores; Q4 FY24 collections Rs.197 crores (91% YoY growth)
items.quote: The collections stood at Rs.570 crores.

items.statement: Strong demand across segments: high-end (Juhu 38% sold pre-completion), mid-affordable (Bangalore), mass (Manhattan 76% sold at podium stage)
items.quote: So, if you really look at the way sales are happening, just to give you an example of Juhu, as I said, usually in the earlier days and when we actually took up the project, in a micro market like Juhu where the project is a little high end, usually these sales are happening towards the completion of the project or once the project is completed. But if you really look at it, we have already sold ab

items.statement: New players entering MMR but established brand and 55-year track record (45,000+ apartments) provide competitive advantage in redevelopment deals
items.quote: People are entering, market is good, so obviously many new players are coming in, and which is good for the market. But most importantly, for us, we are not too worried is primarily because we see that today in spite of there being competition, there has been enough and good demand for established players.

items.statement: Portfolio average realization ~Rs.19,000/sq ft (Rs.1,000+ crores sales / 4+ lakh sq ft); Bangalore Rs.6,000-9,000/sq ft, Mumbai varies by micro-market
items.quote: So, typically like Rs.1,000 crores of sales and having 4 lakhs plus square feet kind of a thing. So, on an average we have about Rs.19,000 as per square feet realization on a portfolio level basis.

items.statement: Diverse portfolio: Wadala (Manhattan, Greenfinity), Ghatkopar (Eden), Juhu (Prive), Bangalore (Lugaano, Florenza), upcoming Kanjurmarg, Bhandup
items.quote: In Mumbai market, we are spending on a very different micro market right from our own land at Wadala to Juhu or to the Pantnagar Eden Project, Greenfinity which is another affordable product at Wadala kind of a thing.

items.statement: Cluster redevelopment requires minimum 4,000 sq meters land; MHADA/cluster redevelopment has 30-year building age criteria
items.quote: It's about 4,000 square meters of land.

items.statement: Pre-sales guidance conservative due to launch timing (majority in Jan-Mar FY25) and phased launch strategy (60% of project value launched, targeting 30-35% sell-through)
items.quote: Now the timing of these projects is going to be anywhere between November to March. So, some will be earlier, some will be towards August, some will be November, and majority of the larger ones are going to be between Jan to March. So, to capture that entire figure in a larger way is going to be difficult, and hence looking all the permutation and combination we have given a guidance of Rs.1,350 c

items.statement: Residential market at 10-year high in CY2023; Mumbai highest sales volume and YoY growth; demand fueled by need for larger spaces and upgraded lifestyle
items.quote: Sales volume in primary markets have grown at an extremely healthy rate since 2020 and it has culminated into a 10 year high in the calendar year 2023. The last quarter, Mumbai has witnessed the highest sales volume and year on year growth all across the Indian metros.

items.statement: Redevelopment deals preferred by societies/slum dwellers due to brand trust, quality, and timeline confidence
items.quote: Now society, slum dwellers, even the cluster people, all of them prefer to have larger branded developers coming and doing their development because, A, they are convinced with the kind of project quality; B, they are convinced with the kind of timeline.

items.statement: Targets FY26 revenue of about 4,000 crores with steady EBITDA margin around 12.5%
items.quote: we aim to achieve a top line of about 4,000 crores while maintaining a steady EBITDA margins at around Sangam (India) Limited 13 th May 2024 12.5% for FY26

items.statement: Denim and Phase 1 synthetic fabric capex completed, yielding benefits from Q1 FY25; Phase 2 synthetic fabric underway; Phase 3 yarn on track for Q1 FY26 completion
items.quote: Denim and Phase 1 of synthetic fabric CAPEX has been successfully completed within the expected timeline and will be yielding benefits from Q1 Financial year 25 and this quarter onwards. Phase 2 of synthetic fabric is currently under way and is progressing as per schedule. Phase 3 of yarn segment is also scheduled and it is on track for completion by Q1 FY26

items.statement: Capacity utilization improved across all segments in Q4 FY24; running at broadly full utilization currently
items.quote: During this quarter, there has been an improvement in capacity utilization under all the segments of the company

items.statement: Exported approximately 160 lakh meters of denim fabric in FY20-23; won Texprocil award for highest denim exports
items.quote: During the year, we exported approximately 160 lakhs meter denim fabric across the world

items.statement: Q4 FY24 EBITDA margin expanded 1.7% QoQ to 10%; targets 12.5% by FY26 driven by value-added mix shift
items.quote: EBITDA margin is at 10%, which is expanded about 1.7% quarter on quarter again

items.statement: Value-added (fabric & garment) share at 53% of revenue in FY24; targets ~60% in 2 years, yarn share to fall from 47% to ~40%
items.quote: Currently, 53% of our product mix comprises of value-added products, and going forward, we are committed to increase this further

items.statement: Slight uptake in demand as sector headwinds reduce; improved price relations across all product segments
items.quote: As the sector headwinds have reduced a little, we are witnessing a slight uptake in demand, reflected in improved price relations across all our product segments

items.statement: Exports 33-40% of revenue across 60+ countries; key markets: Bangladesh, South America, Europe, Turkey, Africa, Egypt, Middle East; expects export share to remain in similar range
items.quote: currently about one third of the business in the company comes from the export market and two third comes from the domestic market

items.statement: Cotton prices at Rs 57-58k per candy, 2% cheaper than international; grid power blended cost Rs 7.25/unit; 10% energy from renewables
items.quote: And it is around 57 to 58,000 rupees is the prices per candy. So it is in the reasonable market

items.statement: Net debt-to-equity comfortable; at 85-90% of peak debt levels; undrawn long-term debt Rs 150-200 cr; peak interest cost in Q4 FY24, expected to decline
items.quote: We can safely say that we are at least about 85-90% at the peak debt levels

items.statement: Working capital borrowing cost blended at around 8%
items.quote: Working capital is between around 8%. Blended

items.statement: Last fundraise Rs 100 cr (60% promoter, 40% non-promoter); no further equity infusion foreseen; well capitalized
items.quote: Last fundraising was about 100 crores where 60% was funded by the promoter and 40% was from a non-promoter entity

items.statement: Maintained 20% dividend for continuity; will work on codified dividend policy
items.quote: So we just tried to maintain continuity. Last year, it could have been a higher number, but since we could see that, you know, margins are going to be under pressure in the future. So we tried to be conservative last year and this year we try to maintain some continuity there

items.statement: FTA talks with UK and Australia advanced; expected to progress after new government forms in a couple of months
items.quote: the very advanced talk with the UK and Australia, but it will take some time with the new government will come into power, right? Probably it will happen in a couple of months time

items.statement: Dyes and chemicals cost (classified in other expenses) rises with fabric turnover increase
items.quote: For example dyes and chemicals used in processing. When our fabric turnover increases the raw material on the processing division is dyes and chemicals but that is classified in other expenses

items.statement: Garment segment ~3% of total revenue; substantial growth expected in FY25 as garment capex completed
items.quote: Currently, Garment consists of about 3% of the total business

items.statement: Interest rates at global peak; any further rate hikes could increase finance cost beyond current peak
items.quote: we are at the peak of the interest rates across the globe. So now that is beyond our control. So whatever easing will happen there, that can contribute

items.statement: 30-40 major clients across segments; details in investor presentation
items.quote: there are about 30-40 big clients that we put on the presentation

items.statement: Competitive advantage from diversified portfolio across cotton/synthetic yarn, denim, synthetic fabric, garment; ability to supply multiple products to brands
items.quote: we are better placed in terms of the varied product ranges and when we are entering some markets where you know we're dealing with brands so we are able to supply various products versus just doing one product there

items.statement: ESOP/Sweat equity issued 2 years ago amortized over 5 years; exceptional item relates to this non-cash cost
items.quote: this is with regards to the the ESOPs and SWEAT equities that that were issued to various company, company officials, I think 2 years back. So that is that that is going to be amortised over 5 years

items.statement: FY25 revenue growth target upwards of 20%
items.quote: We continue to be bullish in terms of our outlook for '25 and expect revenue growth to be upwards of 20%.

items.statement: FY25 consolidated EBITDA margin target high-teens
items.quote: In terms of margins, we are looking at high-teen margins on a consolidated basis.

items.statement: INR75 crore committed for Surat greenfield Phase 1
items.quote: We have also broken ground in our Surat greenfield project and have committed INR75 crores for Phase 1 expansion.

items.statement: Total CAPEX ~INR100 crore over next 1.5 years across Surat, Nadiad, Nashik
items.quote: So overall, between Surat, Nadiad, Nashik, we are looking at about INR100 crores CAPEX.

items.statement: Surat greenfield expected ready in 15 months; existing plants at 70-85% utilisation
items.quote: We have just broken ground. So we expect that factory to be ready within the next 15 months.

items.statement: Soul brand FY24 revenue ~INR3 crore, run-rate INR6 crore, FY25 target INR30 crore
items.quote: Our internal target for this year on Soul is around INR30 crores.

items.statement: Truly Indian brand 3-4% of standalone revenue, targeting Ashoka size in 3-5 years
items.quote: We are looking at anywhere between 3 to 5 years for the Truly Indian brand to get to that.

items.statement: FY24 consolidated EBITDA margin 20.2%, up 230 bps YoY
items.quote: EBITDA margin stood at 20.2%, expanding by 230 basis points Y-o-Y.

items.statement: Q4 FY24 consolidated EBITDA margin 22.3%
items.quote: Our EBITDA margin stood at 22.3%.

items.statement: Standalone FY24 EBITDA margin 24.6%, up 290 bps YoY
items.quote: We managed to expand EBITDA margin by 290 basis points, reaching 24.6%.

items.statement: Red Sea crisis raised freight cost from 7% to 9% of revenue in Q4; rates normalising to 6-7% from April
items.quote: Freight cost was around 7% in the previous quarter for us of the top line, went up to 9% in Q4.

items.statement: Strong demand across all brands; volume and revenue growth near equal in FY24
items.quote: We continue to witness strong demand across all our brands.

items.statement: Processed food share increase drove gross margin improvement in Q4
items.quote: If you also see the processed food as a share of total revenue is also higher compared to the previous quarter. And hence, the gross margins are better in this quarter.

items.statement: Truly Indian listed in 2 new US chains (~300 stores); UK listings with Tesco and Morrison (~300+120 stores)
items.quote: We've got listed in 2 more chains in the U.S., which will give us -- for the Truly Indian brand, we will have some 300 stores from these 2 chain stores.

items.statement: B2B private label 23% of standalone revenue, targeting ~30% in FY25
items.quote: We expect that business to grow in this year and probably we might see another 5% growth. So it might go up to close to 30% in terms of on a standalone basis.

items.statement: Balance sheet debt-free; cash balance ~INR140 crore; not averse to debt if needed
items.quote: Our balance sheet continues to remain debt-free as on date.

items.statement: Business head hired for India; building out India distribution team
items.quote: So we've got a business head for India who is there, and they are building out a team in India for our India distribution.

items.statement: Greenfield Surat plant targets asset turnover >3x (INR250-275 cr revenue on INR75 cr capex)
items.quote: We are spending almost INR75 crores, that's the budget which we have, and it will give us almost a top line of INR250 crores to INR275 crores.

items.statement: Warrant proceeds INR50 crore (2020) deployed in CAPEX over last 3 years
items.quote: This is largely into the CAPEX, which we have done over the last 3 years.

items.statement: In talks with 1-2 FMCG companies for selective agency distribution partnerships
items.quote: We are in talks with 1 or 2 more companies.

items.statement: Germany Truly Indian presence >1,000-1,500 stores; UK ~500-600 stores across 4 chains
items.quote: There, I think our number of stores should be in excess of 1,000 or 1,500 stores where we are there in the major chains out there. U.K., we would be in about, I would say, close to 500 to 600 stores across 4 major supermarket chains there.

items.statement: Soul brand launching 20+ new products in FY25 including frozen foods, sauces, dips
items.quote: In this year, you will see we would have another 20-odd products lined up for India under the Soul brand in this financial year.

items.statement: FY24 CAPEX INR8 crore debottlenecking + INR4 crore cold storage
items.quote: Our CAPEX for FY '24 was INR8 crores in debottlenecking and another INR4 crores in cold storage project.

items.statement: Record quarterly revenue of INR898 crores in Q4 FY24, up double digits YoY driven by rail and domestic sectors; exports down and expected to remain soft short to medium term
items.quote: the highlight of the Q4 '23-'24 performance were that we had a record quarterly revenue of INR898 crores, which were up double digits from last year same time, mostly rail and domestic sector.

items.statement: Export markets not buoyant in short to medium term; heavy truck market soft globally, rail markets in South America robust, North America okay, Australia flattish, ASEAN flat to low, China wind down
items.quote: Unfortunately, the exports were down. And we still see that export markets are not going to be buoyant in short to medium term.

items.statement: Rail order book robust for next 15 months; visibility for full FY25 and into mid-FY26
items.quote: Yes. It looks pretty robust touch wood. And then as we get into October, then our visibility will go into '25 mid till that time.

items.statement: Rail demand sustainable for many years driven by wagon manufacturing, Vande Bharat, metro, locomotive, electrification, dedicated freight corridor, track doubling
items.quote: Rail certainly is going to remain, as I always say, that this rail will always be better than the previous years for many, many years to come.

items.statement: Evaluating rail capacity expansion due to strong domestic and export demand; no decision taken yet but under active consideration
items.quote: Certainly, I think the rail capacity as it goes today and we are also exporting it in some markets at times are being like South America is doing pretty well, And we are looking at these capacities very closely.

items.statement: Process industry (steel, cement, power) to see nice growth; steel per capita consumption low, capacity additions ongoing, Bharuch plant to support
items.quote: So this market will remain pretty nice as we need more steel for building the infra in India. And we -- from the Timken India side will remain close to the customer and we will make sure that we ride the wave as it comes.

items.statement: New Bharuch plant on track; main shop floor completed, pre-engineering building up, roofing and substation work in progress, ERP live, machines arriving, PPAP by end of calendar year, commercial production thereafter
items.quote: likely, production start is same as per plan. So we should be able to -- the machines are either on the seas or landing in Bombay from different parts of the world as this is going to be a high-tech plant with a lot of robotics and IoT and things like that.

items.statement: Q4 margin expansion driven by favorable volume, product mix, better capacity utilization, supply chain cost leverage, and strong price realization despite softening steel prices
items.quote: strong margin performance in the quarter largely was driven by favorable volume and product mix and the better cost leverage we have been trying to do in the area of supply chain.

items.statement: Q4 margin sustainability depends on volume and mix; quarter-to-quarter variation expected; focus on supply chain behavior and volume leverage for profitable growth
items.quote: As I said that it is a volume and mix driven. So, some quarters go up, some quarters come down. So that up and down remains for every company.

items.statement: Q4 FY24 revenue mix: rail 34%, mobile 17%, distribution 19%, process 17%, exports 14%; FY24 full year: rail 23%, mobile 20%, distribution 18%, process 19%, exports 20%
items.quote: For the Q4, our revenue breakup was, rail was 34% in the quarter. And mobile, others was 17% and distribution was 19% and process industry was 17% and the exports were 14%.

items.statement: FY24 vs FY23 mix shift: rail up from 17% to 23%, process up from 16% to 19%, exports down from 28% to 20%, mobile and distribution flat
items.quote: And if you compare this with '22-'23, rail was 17%, and this year -- we completed the pie was 23%. And mobile, others remained flattish 20%-20%, distribution same, 18%-18% and process was 16% in '22-'23 went up to 19%. And the exports came down from 28% in the pie to 20%.

items.statement: Exports bottomed out in Q4 FY24 at 14% of revenue; next quarter slightly better but no hockey-stick recovery; calendar year 2024 expected soft
items.quote: While the next quarter might be a little bit better but the idea of soft landing which was earlier thought that by H2 U.S. market would be up and running with full speed, that is not seen by us.

items.statement: Heavy truck (Class 8) market soft globally including US and India; rail exports to South America robust, North America okay; off-highway US also weak
items.quote: However, on the heavy truck side, it is not where it should be and it is soft. And the soft landing is not expected in the H2. It looks to be in the short and medium term, it will remain soft.

items.statement: Parent company evaluating sourcing/resourcing from India but changes take time; plants in Mexico, US, China also in network
items.quote: So the global supply chain folks are always looking at options of sourcing, resourcing. But as you know that resourcing, changing source it is like steering a very big ship, cannot be done overnight.

items.statement: Jamshedpur running 6 days, 3 shifts (full); Bharuch running near full, ~5% less loaded
items.quote: Jamshedpur is running 6 days full 3 shifts. Bharuch is also running more or less full. We don't see that going down. And Jamshedpur is running flat out.

items.statement: Export contribution target 25-30% of total revenue over next couple of years; domestic priority, China+1 benefit, capacity to follow market
items.quote: Yes. 25%-30%, that is the correct range. But the long answer, definitely, Indian market is growing. And then there is definitely China-PLUS-One, which is going to and is benefitting India.

items.statement: New Bharuch plant (CRB/SRB) focus domestic first, then ASEAN, Australia; currently importing SRB/CRB, domestic production to improve cost structure and grow penetration from single to double digits
items.quote: So currently, we are selling SRB/CRB in India, and we are importing them from different parts of the world. So obviously, when we are domestically producing your structure of the cost would be different

items.statement: Domestic SRB/CRB production expected to have positive margin impact if all else equal
