items.quote: On Pizza Hut, we are seeing improvement compared to what we saw last year. But because the brand is -- has undergone a fragile few quarters, I'm still wanting to see how it pans out. And perhaps before the next -- or during the next quarterly results, we s hould give you concrete evidence that indeed we are starting to turn the corner on the brand

items.statement: Consolidated restaurant EBITDA margin 13.6% in Q4 FY24, down 260 bps YoY; adjusted EBITDA margin 8.6%, down 3% YoY
items.quote: Consolidated restaurant EBITDA declined 5% year -on-year and margin was 13.6%, down 260 basis points. Consolidated EBITDA at INR 110 crores, 17.5%, grew Y -on-Y by 7%. Adjusted EBITDA, that is pre-Ind AS 116, at INR54 crores in the quarter, 8.6%, declined by 3% Y-o-Y.

items.statement: Pizza Hut Q4 FY24 restaurant EBITDA -2.7%; excluding additional marketing spend, brand broke even at restaurant EBITDA level
items.quote: And while gross margins improved year -on-year by 120 bps, the impact of negative SSSG and higher marketing spends meant that the restaurant EBITDA came at negative 2.7%. If we exclude the additional marketing spend done during the year -- during the quarter, the brand broke even at the restaurant EBITDA level.

items.statement: Sri Lanka Q4 FY24 restaurant EBITDA 12.3%, impacted by store operating cost inflation despite gross margin improvement of 90 bps QoQ
items.quote: And while gross margin saw also an improvement even in Lanka business by -- up by 90 basis points quarter-on-quarter, restaurant EBITDA came at 12.3%, impacted by, as Sanjay mentioned, the cost inflation which we experienced on the operating expense side of the store.

items.statement: Pizza Hut added 33 stores in FY24; Q4 FY24 net-zero additions; expansion to remain extremely cautious
items.quote: Last -- with the year gone by, we added 33 restaurants for Pizza Hut. Yes, for the quarter, 0 additions. And for the previous quarter, it was 8. As we called out, the expansion will be c autious. We are not saying we are going to be 0 or pausing completely. It will be extremely cautious, suffice to say

items.statement: Sri Lanka store additions to remain single-digit in FY25 until margins recover to mid-teens
items.quote: You could see it as single digit in terms of a store count addition for the financial year.

items.statement: FY24 capex ~INR 385 crores; KFC capex ~INR 2 cr/store (1,500-1,600 sq ft); Pizza Hut capex ~INR 1.42-1.45 cr/store
items.quote: As I called out previously, if you look at the CapEx per store per format, so KFC CapEx is generally in the ra nge of INR 2 crores per store for around 1,500 to 1,600 square feet. Pizza Hut, we are seeing it in the range of INR 1.42 crores to 1.45 crores per store on Pizza Hut.

items.statement: Gross margins improved 150 bps YoY for KFC and 120 bps for Pizza Hut in Q4 FY24; expect gross margins to range +/- 2 bps sequentially going forward; no material price increases expected
items.quote: So whatever benefit had to come in into the P&L in terms of gross margin improvement, I think that's locked largely starting Q3 of last year. And if you see sequential gross margin, we had called out that it will be ranged from plus/minus 2 basis points. I think going forward, we expect that the gross margins would be ranged about plus/minus 2 basis points. And we don't see any price increase -- m

items.statement: KFC launched 5 new burgers (American, Caribbean, Mexican, Indian veg/non-veg) and relaunched Chizza LTO and paneer Zinger in Q4 FY24
items.quote: And this quarter, we've taken our burger game to the next level by launching 5 new burgers: American, Caribbean, Mexican, Indian and Indian veg and Indian nonveg. We've re launched also, which you will discover only at the store, the Indian veg option, a paneer Zinger.

items.statement: New fried chicken entrants (Popeyes, Wow Chicken) create positive category noise; KFC's scale and sourcing economies protect margins; unlikely competitors can sustain price leadership
items.quote: So in that sense, competition is only good. Now the second part to that question is that however, at the scale that KFC operates, we undoubtedly have economies of scale also. So it is difficult for any competitor to come in and be a cost leader and, therefore, impair margins. So I don't think that should happen, point number two.

items.statement: KFC SSSG -3% in Q4 FY24; ADS INR 114,000 (impacted by ~25% new store additions which operate at 70-80% of brand average in year 1)
items.quote: SSSG came at minus 3%. Our ADS is at INR114,000. Just to clarify, the ADS is also impacted by new store additions, which we're, over the year almost at 25% restaurant additions. And as we called out, generally, the new stores take time to scale up. And their ADS are generally lower initially the first year compared to the brand average.

items.statement: No specific debt commentary; consolidated PBT INR 80 lakhs (0.1%), adjusted PBT INR 8.3 cr (1.3%) in Q4 FY24
items.quote: Consolidated PBT of INR8 million or INR80 lakhs, or 0.1%. Adjusted PBT was INR8.3 crores or 1.3%.

items.statement: Demand environment soft; seasonal calendar shifts (Navratri, Adhik Maas, Shravan) make quarterly trends noisy; annual view preferred for KFC
items.quote: unfortunately, over the last 3 to 4 years post COVID, every year and every quarter that there has been some of the other exceptions. As a result the trends, which are sequential trends or year -on-year trends, some quarters where it gives out a good picture, some quarters, they are not strictly comparable.

items.statement: Ranked top 3 franchisee by Yum! on customer metrics and operating standards for both KFC and Pizza Hut; #1 QSR in India on ESG (Dow Jones Sustainability Index), 95th percentile globally; best-ever employee engagement score at 88th percentil
items.quote: We are ranked among the top 3 franchisees by Yum! on -- in both KFC as well as Pizza Hut on our customer metrics and our operating standards. We're also quite proud that we were ranked the number 1 QSR in India on our ESG score rated by Dow Jones Sustainability Index, and we are 95th percentile among all QSRs globally. We also achieved -- this is an internal metric, but I'd like to share with you.

items.statement: Appointed new CFO Munish Gupta (CA, IIM Ahmedabad, 20 years experience) and new COO Mukul Khanna (25 years in consumer durables, telecom, e-commerce)
items.quote: I am accompanied by our new CFO, Mr. Munish Gupta. He is a CA and an Executive MBA from IIM Ahmedabad with 20 years of expertise in construction, hotels, IT travel, start-ups, and FMCG.

items.statement: Appointed new COO Mukul Khanna with 25 years experience in consumer durables, telecom, and e-commerce
items.quote: In addition, we have appointed a new Chief Operating Officer, Mr. Mukul Khanna, a 25-year business leader in consumer durables, telecom, and e-commerce.

items.statement: Q4 FY24 revenue grew 21.7% YoY to INR252.5 crores; FY24 revenue grew 26.7% to INR999 crores
items.quote: Revenue from operations is up by 26.7% to INR 999 crores from INR 788 crores in FY '23.

items.statement: FY24 EBITDA grew 36% to INR175.3 crores with 17.1% margin; PAT grew 38.1% to INR83.3 crores at 8.1% margin
items.quote: EBITDA grew by 36% to INR175.3 crores. EBITDA margin stood at 17.1%. PAT grew by 38.1% to INR83.3 crores. PAT margin for FY '24 stood at 8.1%.

items.statement: Inventory days stood at 161 days as of March 31, 2024; cash and bank balance at INR345.5 crores
items.quote: Inventory days as of March 31 stood at 161 days. Cash and bank balance stood at INR345.5 crores as on March 31, 2024.

items.statement: EFTA agreement will phase out Swiss watch customs duty from 20% to 0% over 7 years, starting H2 FY25 with ~3% annual reduction
items.quote: Custom Duty on Swiss watches is currently at 20% and 2% CESS on that. Under the EFTA agreement, duty on Swiss watches will be reduced to 0 in a 7-year period. This change is likely to start in the second half of this financial year with a 3% decrease in duty every year.

items.statement: EFTA duty reduction expected to improve gross margins and attract more luxury brands to India
items.quote: This will improve Ethos' gross margins. More importantly, it will open doors for many more luxury brands to come in, for whom these rates were a deterrent to profitability and therefore, an Indian presence.

items.statement: Store count increased from 54 stores in 20 cities to 63 stores in 24 cities in FY24; added Surat, Bhubaneshwar, Raipur, Mohali and Breitling boutiques in Pune
items.quote: We started FY '24 with 54 stores in 20 cities, and we currently have 63 stores in 24 cities. We added new cities such as Surat, Bhubaneshwar, Raipur, M ohali and Breitling boutiques at Pune

items.statement: Spent INR38.3 crores on new store fit-outs and restoration in FY24
items.quote: In FY '24, we spent INR38.3 crores on the fit-out of new stores and restoration of existing ones.

items.statement: Exclusive brands accounted for nearly 29% of total sales from portfolio of 51 brands; target 50% revenue from exclusive brands long-term
items.quote: In FY '24, exclusive brands accounted for nearly 29% of our total sales from our portfolio of 51 brands.

items.statement: Same-store sales growth (SSG) was 10% for Q4 FY24
items.quote: SSG is 10% for the quarter.

items.statement: Volume growth of 19% for watches above INR1 lakh (18,471 in FY23 to 22,000 in FY24); exiting sub-INR1 lakh fashion category
items.quote: FY '23, we sold 18,471 watches above INR1 lakh. In FY '24, we sold 22,000 watches, an increase of 19%.

items.statement: Average price increase of 7-8% in Q1 FY25; most brands priced around INR92-93 CHF/INR, exclusive brands at ~INR100
items.quote: The average price increase in the first quarter was roughly about 7% to 8%. Most brands are priced around the INR92 mark.

items.statement: Target 18-20% return on capital in first year for new stores; most boutiques profitable from year one
items.quote: We try to touch 18% to 20% return on capital in the first year itself. That's how we target it.

items.statement: Lifestyle division: RIMOWA Mumbai store profitable from month 1; signing 2 more RIMOWA boutiques (Delhi Emporio, Bangalore Mall of Asia) for H2 FY25 or early FY26
items.quote: Our first store in Mumbai is doing quite well. As we said recently in all -- in our most recent results call, it has been profitable on a PAT basis since month 1.

items.statement: Opening first QlockTwo luxury clocks boutique at UB City Bangalore; actively seeking flagship Messika boutique; discussing brands with $700-800M global turnover
items.quote: We will open our first boutique this year for luxury clocks at UB City in Bangalore, with a brand known as QlockTwo. We are now actively -- also now actively looking for our first flagship boutique for Messika in the country.

items.statement: Second service centre in Bengaluru to be operational in Q2 FY25; Delhi service centre performing well
items.quote: We now plan to open a second service centre in Bengaluru, which will be operational in the second quarter of this year, allowing us to expand our geographic footprint for service.

items.statement: Pre-owned CPO billing was INR66 crores in FY24; committed to growing this business with manpower and training investments
items.quote: Billing from pre-owned CPO was INR66 crores in FY '24.

items.statement: Election Model Code of Conduct subdues April-May sales due to cash movement restrictions and event limitations; June expected strong; April went well, May doing well
items.quote: Every time there are elections, the 2 months leading up to the election are a little bit subdued, and we see great numbers in the months after it. This is because of typically a couple of things. Number one is the Model Code of Conduct, which comes into play and restricts cash movement.

items.statement: Kochi store (5,000 sq ft) opening ~July 1; 6 boutiques at Mall of Asia Bangalore delayed pending luxury floor handover; Dehradun in 45 days; Bangalore airport duty-free in 60 days; Mangalore before H2; flagship City of Time around Diwali
items.quote: Kochi, which is our -- it's a 5,000 square feet boutique will open around the 1st of July. We already have another store in Pune that is already opened. We have 6 boutiques which are lined up for opening in Mall of Asia, Bangalore. That's the landmark boutique mall coming up from

items.statement: Transferred Favre Leuba stake to KDDL to focus on retail; KDDL to handle manufacturing; Ethos retains ~30% stake to influence brand strategy for India; target 50% revenue from exclusive brands
items.quote: Ethos will focus upon India. Ethos' core competency is retail in India, right? Our long-term goal is to reach 50% of our brands coming where we have exclusivity and through strategic tie-up, right?

items.statement: Investing in HR professionalization, training school for shop floor talent, design and tech teams to support 10-year 10x revenue goal
items.quote: The need for the hour to achieve the 10-year goal of 10x revenue is to get great talent at every level. We will make investments into our training school for talent on the shop floor as well as investments into engagement of the HR to lower attrition.

items.statement: No short-term guidance going forward; focusing on long-term strategies and 10-year vision after 2 years of quarterly guidance
items.quote: These earnings call now represent 2 years of earnings calls since we listed. We have given short-term guidance till now to guide investors and increase stability. We will now focus on long-term strategies and long-term visions instead of just focusing on giving short-term guidance.

items.statement: CHF/INR forex: started FY24 at INR92, peaked at INR99 in Dec'23, back to INR92; Q4 forex gain INR1.3 crores; full year forex loss INR1 crore
items.quote: The CHF to INR at the start of the year was INR92. At in December '23, it was INR99, which was not seen historically. And again, now it's INR92. In terms of overall forex gain in Q4, we are positive by INR1.3 crores. And for the full year, the overall forex's, there is a loss of INR1 crore.

items.statement: Launching app and overhauling website for better UI/UX, personalization, concierge service; deploying AI with 4 use cases including proprietary LLMs for visual search and customer presentations
items.quote: With the launch of the app and an upcoming overhaul of the website, we will focus on better user interaction, UI/UX, digital journey personalization and better service provided by our concierge with the help of technology.

items.statement: Target loan book growth of 22-24% for FY25 and 22-25% CAGR over next 3-5 years
items.quote: we are looking for a growth for FY '25, a growth of 22% to 24% on the advanced book si de. And going forward also, we want to look to increase our loan growth on a CAGR of 22% to 25% over the next three to five years

items.statement: Target ROTA expansion to 1.4% for FY25 with continuous improvement thereafter
items.quote: We target ROTA expansion to 1.4% for FY'25 and continuous ROTA expansion going forward.

items.statement: Opex ratio expected to remain around current FY24 level of 2.95% in FY25
items.quote: We believe our opex ratio going forward will remain around the same level as in the current fiscal year.

items.statement: Plan to add 25+ branches in FY25 to cross 200 total branches
items.quote: Post the growth capital pouring in, we are intending to scale up our branch expansion by adding 25 plus branches and we want to cross our branch count by end of this year to 200 plus.

items.statement: Target medium-term CD ratio in mid to high 80s from current 79%
items.quote: So we typically look for the medium term range to take it mid to the high 80s.

items.statement: NIM for FY24 was 3.9%; expect expansion via CD ratio improvement and loan repricing
items.quote: The NIM for the year is 3.9% and our non-interest income is 0.8% against 0.6% a year before.

items.statement: 35-40% of floating rate book to reprice in Q1 FY25 after 35 bps MCLR hike in FY24
items.quote: Now we believe around our 35% to 40% of the book will be starting repricing in quarter one only of FY '25 so which will be giving us a benefit as we move forward.

items.statement: Cost of deposits stabilized at 7.55-7.65% retail rate; expect stable cost of funds
items.quote: our offered rate on retail deposit is now constant over the last, for a while, say six months to nin e months. That is the almost similar rates. We believe the rate of deposit, cost of deposit is getting optimized

items.statement: Gross advances at INR 6,160 crore as of March 31, 2024 with 19% 5-year CAGR
items.quote: Our gross advances stood at INR 6160 crores as on March 31, registering 5-year CAGR of 19%, Q-o-Q growth of 8% and Y-o-Y growth of 12% respectively.

items.statement: FY24 disbursements INR 2,068 crore; Q4 FY24 disbursements INR 675 crore (76% QoQ growth)
items.quote: Our disbursements for FY24 were INR 2,068 crores consisting of around 27% to agriculture, 24%-25% to mortgage, 22%-23% to MSME and trading segment.

items.statement: GNPA 2.8%, NNPA 1.4% in FY24; slippage ratio 2.4%, upgrade/recovery 2.1%
items.quote: We have industry leading asset quality with GNPA and NNPA off 2.8% and 1.4% respectively. Our NNPA is stable around the same level over the last 3 years.

items.statement: PCR maintained at 50%+; near-zero write-offs and nil NPA sell-off since inception
items.quote: Our provision coverage ratio for the current period is around 50% and we are maintaining almost similar type of PCR over the period.

items.statement: SMA 1+2 at 4.5% of portfolio; 90%+ recovery via standing instruction route
items.quote: If we look into SMA 1 and 2, which put together is 4.5%. SMA 0 being 0 to 30 days is one segment given we being using our own accounts for recovery and our 90% plus recovery through SI route.

items.statement: Branch expansion to 200+ branches in FY25; majority outside Punjab
items.quote: We are presently having 177 branches spread over 5 states and 1 union territory of Chandigarh. Post the growth capital pouring in, we are intending to scale up our branch expansion by adding 25 plus branches and we want to cross our branch count by end of this year to 200 plus.

items.statement: Regional/cluster and head office infrastructure ready to support 225-250 branches from current 177
items.quote: We have the regional cluster and head office level readiness t o support up to 225 to 250 branches from 177

items.statement: Deposit rates stable at 7.55-7.65% for retail; MCLR increased 35 bps in FY24 (20 bps in Q4)
items.quote: During FY '24 our deposit rate remain almost at the same level throughout beginning of the year and at the end of the year with our highest rate of deposit for retail was around 7.55% to 7.65%. At the end of the year also it is 7.55 % to 7.65% and if we look into the MCLR we have increased the MCLR by 35 basi s points during FY '24 out of which 20 basi s point increase in the Q4 FY '24

items.statement: Quarterly pattern: Q1/Q3 deposit-heavy, Q2/Q4 advance-heavy due to SURU branch mix (74%)
items.quote: If you look into our historical trends, you will find our Q1 will be heavy on deposit growth, Q2 being heavy on our advanced growth, Q3 being heavy on our deposit growth, Q4 being our heavy on the advanced growth.

items.statement: On track for universal bank license; meet all criteria except net NPA <1% (currently 1.4%); target 12-18 months
items.quote: If we look into that particular guidelines, we have complied with all the requirements except net NPA, which is prescribed to be 1%. We believe that given our plan going ahead, keeping in view the macroeconomic factors which are prevailing as on date, we intend to achieve that over the next 12 to 18-month period.

items.statement: No significant impact from farmer protests on recoveries or asset quality; minimal historical impact
items.quote: Whether we took into from the perspective of the growth rate or from the asset qualityyou can see there is no impact of the same. Yes, we believe strongly as a corporate , this thing should settle quickly. But presently we are not seeing any significant impact on it on our balance sheet and the book

items.statement: ECL framework adoption expected to have positive impact (reduced provision requirement)
items.quote: As far as the last calculation which we have done on the ECL, we are finding a positive impact on the reduced ECL provision requirement as per the performance.

items.statement: Dividend payout 4% of profit; board decision balancing growth capital retention and investor cash flow
items.quote: So, this is a decision of my board. So, being a growth-oriented organization / we being in a growth engine-based organization, which will necessitating to sow a seed for our future growth. So, this is as part of that strategy that we continue to sow a seed for our future growth and keep on keeping/retaining the profit/money with us.

items.statement: CASA ratio 38%+ (retail CASA 41%+); retail deposits 92.9% of total deposits
items.quote: If we look into our CASA number if you slice it further and divide it with our deposit which is retail deposit you will find still our retail CASA deposit is 41% plus which is almost a similar level which was a year back.

items.statement: Staff cost 55-60% of opex; no significant middle management hiring needed for 225-250 branch capacity
items.quote: Our overall opex ratio, given staff cost and other staff cost, that is the split which we are talking about is typically, we are typically maintaining 55% to 60% in one of the segment, being 40% to 45% being other segment.

items.statement: FY25 consolidated revenue guidance of Rs.675 crores (~30% growth)
items.quote: I am pleased to inform you that we are expecting close to 30% growth this year and achieve a combined revenue of Rs.675 crores.

items.statement: FY28 revenue target of over Rs.1000 crores
items.quote: we aim to now double our Jash Engineering Limited revenue to over Rs.1000 crores FY28 that is in four years time

items.statement: EBITDA margin target of 23-24% over time
items.quote: As I have been informing all the investors over the last few years, we are quite hopeful of increasing our EBITDA margin up to 23-24% in time to come to come.

items.statement: PAT margin target range of 12-14%
items.quote: As already informed by me before that we expect PAT margins to grow between 12-14% in time to come.

items.statement: Combined order book of Rs.816 crores (excl. Waterfront) as of FY24 end
items.quote: Our combined orderbook is Rs.816 crore of which business outside India is Rs.551 crores and within India is Rs.265 crores.

items.statement: Waterfront UK order book ~Rs.30 crores; 80% consolidation adds Rs.225-235 crores
items.quote: This Rs.816 crores does not include the current order booking of Waterfront UK. This current order booking is close to Rs.30 crores and we hope that when 80% of this order book of Waterfront is added to the combine orderbook we are looking at something like Rs.225-235 crores as our combined order book including Waterfront.

items.statement: Negotiated orders Rs.31 crores and under negotiation Rs.33 crores as of 1st May (excl. large tickets)
items.quote: As on 1st May our orders which we have already negotiated and which we expect to receive are of Rs.31 crores and orders under negotiations are also around Rs.33 crores and t his does not include marqu ee big orders which are under negotiation

items.statement: Annual capex of Rs.20-25 crores for next 2-3 years
items.quote: Every year somewhere between Rs.20-25 crores. So, every year we will be investing Rs.20-25 crores to add some facility and this will keep on happening for next 2-3 years.

items.statement: Current manufacturing potential ~Rs.800 crores; targeting Rs.1000 crores with new plants
items.quote: with all these facilities whi ch we own now, our turnover potential has come to around Rs.800 crores. So, we are committed to build facility as we grow, with Rs.800 crores facility we would be able to sustain till next year. However, once we again add new facilities in SEZ next year we intend to take this capacity up to Rs.1000 crores in a year or two

items.statement: New stainless steel plant at Unit II commissioned Dec 2023; Waterfront Glasgow plant commissioning first week of June 2024; Shivpad Chennai plant by Dec 2024; SEZ Unit IV extension by Oct-Nov 2025
items.quote: In this year, in December one plant will come online in Chennai and in May a plant to come online in UK which means I have two plants being added this year and one plant which will be added next year sometime in October November. So, with these three plants, we will exceed Rs.1000 crores manufacturing capability.

items.statement: FY24 consolidated gross margin 59.7%, EBITDA margin 20.2% (up from 18.6%), PAT margin 12.8% (up from 12.5%)
items.quote: In FY24 our gross profit margin has been 59.7% . T he EBITDA and EBITDA margin also sho ws much improvement in this year, last year was 18.6% this year is 20.2

items.statement: Rodney Hunt PAT grew >110%; Waterfront PAT margin ~3-4% targeting >10% in 2-3 years
items.quote: The margins at Waterfront are not great, because the revenue is not great. But we expect margin profile of Waterfront to improve over the years and come to the same level as Jash and Rodney Hunt in time to come. I would say now the margins are close to 3-4% and year on year we expect 3-4% growth so that in next 2-3 years time they have more than 10% margins.

items.statement: Water reuse market in India expected to become significant by 2027-29; Invent product line targets Rs.75-125 crores in India
items.quote: I would say, i f we do everything right, we are looking at anywhere between Rs.75-125 crores

items.statement: Southeast Asia order book >Rs.100 crores; entering Vietnam, Laos, Cambodia, Indonesia; Thailand revenue projection $2-3M
items.quote: The orderbook is still great. We have more than Rs.100 crores of orders for Southeast Asia.

items.statement: New products (Invent line, disc filter, bladder vessel, vortex grit classifier) to contribute 10-15% of revenue in 4 years
items.quote: So, 10-15% new products will contribute once they get stabilize. For new product to launch is very easy , for ne w products to capture the market and become a dominant player takes time, 4-5 years

items.statement: FY24 ex-India revenue ~60%; UK Waterfront targeting 5-6x growth to Rs.200 crores in 4 years
items.quote: We are planning 18-20 million pounds like Rs.200 crores in four year time. So, from Rs.35 crores today.

items.statement: Three large international orders (Hong Kong, Canada, USA) totalling $50-60M with >75% win probability
items.quote: So, we are as of now working on three large orders. One in Hong Kong, one in Canada and one in America. All the three orders put together we are talking of more than $50-60 million.

items.statement: Government approved Jash technology for all hydropower plants under new small hydro policy
items.quote: on those interactions the government has now in their new small hydro policy approved our technology for all the hydropower plants

items.statement: Working capital cycle ~100-110 days when averaged across quarters
items.quote: If you average it out through all the four quarters, then will realise our working capital cycle is not more than 100-110 days.

items.statement: Tax rate currently 20-22% (100% SEZ exemption), rising to 24-25% after 50% exemption; US losses fully absorbed
items.quote: This year we only got 100% exemption in SEZ unit IV after that we will have 50%. So, at present our tax level will be 20-22% but later on its around 24-25%. In US we have already absorbed all losses.

items.statement: Waterfront UK acquisition completed; 80% owned; share issuance done April 2024; Scottish Enterprise grant 75,000 GBP received
items.quote: Its was done in April 2024.

items.statement: Employee retention initiatives: ESOP, sports turf, restaurant, campus investments to attract talent
items.quote: ESOP, turf cricket, restaurant, employee engagement activities, good campuses are all part of that.

items.statement: Rodney Hunt order book $43M; FY25 revenue target $35M (up from $26.5M)
items.quote: We already have order book of $43 million in Rodney Hunt. So, it means that next year also Rodney Hunt would grow by more than 30%.

items.statement: India addressable market Rs.800-900 crores currently; 30% of wastewater capacity built, 70% pending
items.quote: So, Rs.800-900 crores was our addressable market in India. Now this can increase if t he government increase the spending on water and wastewater

items.statement: Revenue recognition dependent on EPC contractor delivery schedules; global events (war, crisis) could derail guidance
items.quote: Most of the time we are dependent on EPC contract or, we may produce an email not a delivery. So, in spite of having orders, we may not achieve the desired targeted revenue.

items.statement: >70% market share in gates in India; competitors are small; detailed competitor list in website FAQ
items.quote: For gates, by the way gates we have more than 70% market share in India. So, there are very small companies turnover wise who are our competitors.

items.statement: Discrete manufacturing model: capacity utilisation skewed to H2 (Q4 40% of revenue); adding shifts/people can increase throughput
items.quote: in the first quarter revenue is 10%, in the first half the revenue is 30% , in the third quarter the revenue is 60% and the last quarter the revenue is 100

items.statement: JLR expects EBIT margin around FY24 level (8.5%) for FY25, investment spend ~GBP 3.5bn, net debt zero target by year-end, Q1 cash flow broadly breakeven
items.quote: we expect EBIT margin for this year to be around the level of FY 2024. We expect investment spend to be around GBP 3.5 billion, and we are holding our target to be net debt zero by the end of this ﬁnancial year

items.statement: Tata Motors capex for next year broadly similar to FY24 at Rs 8,300 Cr, JLR capex ~GBP 3.5bn
items.quote: is well funded by the operating cash, and nothing abnormal there. And the investment spending, we ended the year at Rs. 8,300 Cr. There are some sure questions, I already see what is likely to be JLR's investment and what is ours - about GBP 3.5 billion in JLR and broadly similar lines for Tata Motors

items.statement: Consolidated FY24 revenue grew ~27%, EBITDA 14.3%, EBIT 8.3%, PBT before exceptional ~Rs 29,000 Cr, auto free cash flow Rs 27,000 Cr

items.quote: Simone itself, we expect about INR25 crores minimum turnover to happen in FY '25. And then we hope that this will continue to double every year.

items.statement: Gradual industry recovery expected in FY25 driven by domestic demand revival, export recovery, and lower raw material prices.
items.quote: A gradual recovery at an industry level is expected in the next financial year '25, and on the back of improvements in sales realizations and stabilized raw material costs.

items.statement: USA market showing strong interest and new customers joining; expects to recover close to prior year levels.
items.quote: U.S.A. is showing a lot of interest now. We lost 56% compared to last year in the U.S.A. market. And we expect now to recover and get pretty close to where we were last year in the U.S.A. market again.

items.statement: EBITDA margin lower in FY24 due to subdued demand and inventory correction after COVID over-ordering; aims for double-digit margin in FY25.
items.quote: The reason is that everybody in the financial year '24 had the subdued demand and the latent demand after COVID and had ordered more than they thought.

items.statement: Endeavors to reach double-digit EBITDA margin in FY25, subject to market dynamics.
items.quote: Aditya, yes, endeavors are there to really get into the double digit for surely. Also, it has external effect and the constraints from the market also.

items.statement: Order cycles: Fabric ~60 days, Garment ~90 days, Yarn ~30 days; uniform orders have longer projections.
items.quote: Otherwise, generally, the order cycling for fabric is around 60 days. 60 days before they need it, they tell you that this is a fabric order. For Garment, it's is usually 90 days and for Yarn, it's usually 30 days.

items.statement: No significant capex needed to reach INR 2,000 crore turnover; considering third automotive textile unit in Madhya Pradesh.
items.quote: We have one in Banswara, and we are considering a third in Madhya Pradesh.

items.statement: Raw material costs stabilized; cotton prices falling but pricing under pressure; linen and wool prices rising.
items.quote: With the cotton prices falling, I think that will continue to remain good. The only problem is the pricing is now under pressure in the cotton and the natural fibers.

items.statement: Focus on high-value yarn products, synthetic/wool blends, technical synthetics, flame retardant curtains, tent fabric, automotive textiles, sportswear.
items.quote: We will continue to focus on high-value yarn products that will lead to enhancing value growth along with the overall top line.

items.statement: Bangladesh and Vietnam compete only in garments; FTAs needed to compete; Banswara's strength in yarn/fabric and sustainability compliance gives edge.
items.quote: So when you speak of Bangladesh and Vietnam, they're only doing garments, right? our bigger business is yarn and fabric. The garment part, you are correct that because unless we get FTAs, there's no way to compete.

items.statement: Hopeful for UK FTA to significantly enhance garment business outlook.
items.quote: On the regulatory front, we are hopeful that the U.K. free trade agreement happens, and that would significantly enhance the company's business outlook on Garment.

items.statement: Exports declined to 42% of revenue in FY24 from 48% in FY23; sequential recovery of 31% in Q4 FY24 driven by UAE and European uniform orders.
items.quote: The exports have declined to42% of the overall revenues in FY '24 as compared with the 48% in last year for the same period, mainly due to decline in export of more than 50% in key markets of Europe, Turkey, U.S. and the U.K.

items.statement: Inventory days reduced from 185 to ~175 days; debtor days cyclical; working capital borrowings lowered.
items.quote: Working capital cycle on the inventory side, if you look at, there is a reduction of a number of days coming from the previous year to this year. So now the inventory cycle goes like, okay, it's 175 days kind of average, which we were at 185.

items.statement: Working capital borrowings reduced due to improved working capital cycle.
items.quote: And that's the reason like our borrowings have also, on the working capital side, was lowered.

items.statement: Tesca JV (automotive textiles) turned profitable, paid tax first time; sales INR 80-100 crore range, 20% drop in FY24 but strong profitability.
items.quote: Tesca actually has the sales in the ranging from INR80 crores to INR100 crores. Like in FY '23, they did touch near to INR100 crores, like INR99.8 crores, so they were near to INR100 crores.

items.statement: Synthetic fiber consumption growing faster than cotton globally; technical synthetics (moisture management, performance fabrics) driving future demand.
items.quote: Synthetics is growing now faster than cotton. And the wool part is more ceremonial and for weddings and is more aimed at the upper end of the market.

items.statement: Geopolitical uncertainties, inflation impacting discretionary spending, inventory overhang, and lack of FTAs for garment exports remain key risks.
items.quote: The global economic climate remains challenging with geopolitical uncertainties dampening consumer confidence and impacting global trade.

items.statement: Enhanced travel budgets, larger marketing team, digital marketing tools adopted to explore new geographies.
items.quote: Travel budgets have been enhanced. We have a larger team available, and we are using all sorts of tools of digital marketing in terms of digitizing the product.

items.statement: Middleweight segment expected to grow in double digits; premiumisation theme continuing in India; motorcycle industry slowly returning to pre-COVID levels month-on-month
items.quote: What we can say is the two-wheeler market is poised for a growth, and especially the middleweight. We anticipate the middleweight growth will be in double-digit.

items.statement: Himalayan 450 currently clocking 200-plus motorcycles a day; preparing for higher numbers given global potential; supply ramp-up ongoing for domestic and international markets
items.quote: As far as the Himalayan is concerned, we launched and it has been a super hit for us and happy to share with you, it's beyond the expectation of the numbers, which we are talking about.

items.statement: New products lined up on 450cc Sherpa Platform and 650cc platform; platforms grouped to address different consumer segments with differentiated experiences
items.quote: We have currently three platforms. We have our super refined J-platform. Then we have our 450cc platform, which is the Sherpa Platform and the 650cc platform.

items.statement: Focus on absolute EBITDA increase rather than percentages; international market share recovery and non-motorcycle business growth accretive; monitoring commodity prices but no significant pressure currently
items.quote: First of all, revenue growth itself is something that we are actually focused on. We're looking at absolute increase as far as EBITDA is concerned. We're not necessarily so focused on percentages, as you know.

items.statement: No recent price hike for Royal Enfield; VECV focusing on discount reduction rather than MRP increases to improve transaction prices
items.quote: Royal Enfield side, we haven't taken the price hike very recently. VECV, Vinod? Vinod Aggarwal: In VECV, we are focusing more and more on the discount reduction

items.statement: Commodity prices stable currently; not a headwind or tailwind; tracking PGMs and working on value engineering to offset costs; pricing decisions based on price-value proposition for consumer
items.quote: Commodities, it is not a headwind as of now. Is it a tailwind? May not be. So to that extent, there is some amount of stability, which is there.

items.statement: Export retail sales strong across all markets globally; wholesale picking up slowly; long-term strategy focused on brand building, community, own subsidiaries and CKD plants in key markets
items.quote: international market, Jinesh? Jinesh Gandhi: Yes. B. Govindarajan: No. In the last quarter also I was just telling, we don't track the wholesale. Wholesale is only a transaction number for us. We always look at retail

items.statement: Export strategy divided into richer Western markets (strong profitability, salience) and high-potential LatAm/Southeast Asia markets aiming to create 'mini Indias' with deep penetration over 5-15 years
items.quote: We divided in our export markets into two. One is the richer countries, such as U.S., Europe, Australia, Japan, New Zealand, Korea, where the markets are there, they're not growing, maybe even declining, but affordability is very strong.

items.statement: CV industry has good growth potential driven by 7%+ GDP growth, strong infrastructure programme, and pent-up replacement demand for new technology trucks enhancing productivity
items.quote: As far as the demand for commercial vehicle market is concerned, I think it has got a very good potential for growth. Fundamentally, because our economy is continuing to do well, and of course, we are expecting on the back of around 6% to 8% of last year, we are expecting that this year also the economy should grow by 7% plus.

items.statement: E-bus products ready (9m, 12m, 13.5m intercity); electric truck traction good with 75 sold last year; small commercial EV on pilot with 10 customers, commercial launch from January next year followed by diesel/CNG variants
items.quote: As far as the trucks are concerned, we were the first one to introduce electric truck in 5.5 tonne category. And last year, we have sold 75 electric trucks. And this year, of course, the traction is good.

items.statement: VECV Q4 margin decline YoY due to one-off fiscal incentives accrued last year in Madhya Pradesh; no other reasons for margin decline QoQ despite volume growth
items.quote: Basically, last year in Q4, there were some fiscal incentives, which we had accrued based on the very old, which were pending in Madhya Pradesh. So due to that, there was one-off in last year Q4.

items.statement: Royal Enfield finance penetration at 61% and steadily growing; digital finance marketplace integrated; REOWN upgrade programme piloted in few cities, slowly gaining traction with dealership ecosystem
items.quote: Our finance penetration, as of now is about 61%. It's steadily growing over the period of time. I mean because when the demography is coming down, it also is quite natural that the finance penetration will be there.

items.statement: Replacement cycle for Royal Enfield yet to kick in but preparing with REOWN platform for 6 million vehicle park; focus on frictionless upgrade experience rather than pushing new motorcycles
items.quote: You touched upon the topic of the replacement cycle. In the last call, also I mentioned, it is yet to kick in. But we have to be prepared. So what we have done is to give a very frictionless experience for those consumers almost about 6 million motorcycles, which are there in the market as a vehicle park.

items.statement: Royal Enfield sold 912,000 motorcycles in FY24 (highest ever), up from 834,700 in FY23; 30% market share in 125cc+ category; 7.2% overall motorcycle market share
items.quote: For the financial year, as Siddhartha mentioned, we sold about 912,000 motorcycles, which is compared to last year, which was only about 8,34,700 motorcycles. This is our highest ever volumes in the country, India.

items.statement: VECV sold 85,560 units in FY24 (7.5% growth vs industry 4%); heavy-duty truck market share 9.2% (up from 4% industry growth); light/medium-duty market share 34.7% (market dropped 5.9%)
items.quote: For the full-year, we had 85,560 units as against last full-year of 79,623 units. So with a growth of 7.5% for the full-year. If you look at the industry, industry had grown by 4%.

items.statement: Oragadam plant awarded future-ready factory by Frost & Sullivan; plants creating benchmarks in efficiency, automation and manufacturing excellence; produced 9.2 lakh motorcycles (highest ever)
items.quote: On manufacturing, just to add, we have produced 9.2 lakh motorcycle this year, which is, once again, highest ever production with high quality fit and finish motorcycles for the globe.

items.statement: All VECV vehicles comply with BS-VI OBD2 standards; working on H2ICE technology, hydrogen fuel cells, CNG and LNG trucks; aiming to reduce water usage per vehicle by 5%
items.quote: And all our existing digital vehicles, they comply with all the strict current BS-VI, OBD2 standards. And then, of course, we are committed to increase the use of renewable energy and energy efficiency at our plants and operations.

items.statement: Achieved zero liquid discharge in all operations; all plants and warehouses net water positive (Oragadam index 3.23, Vallam 2.02); 35% renewable energy consumption; on track for 20% carbon emission reduction vs last year; motorcycle reusabi
items.quote: We have achieved zero liquid discharge in all our operations and all our plants and our warehouses are all net water positive, with an index of almost 3.23 in Oragadam and 2.02 in Vallam. We have been constantly working on improving the renewable energy usage. And during this year, further, we enhanced that, and we have 35% of total consumption onto the renewable energy.

items.statement: International market macro situation varies by market; not all markets recovering simultaneously; cautious approach to e-bus tenders under PM-eBus Sewa due to difficult payment model (per km for 12 years)
items.quote: But of course, we will be very careful, not putting in the bids to pursue the volumes at any cost. So therefore, we will see that what makes sense for us. But of course, as far as the products are concerned, we are all ready with the 9-meter bus product, 12-meter bus product, and we are also going to introduce 13.5-meter intercity bus product.

items.statement: FY25 deposit growth guided at 10-12% with focus on CASA and retail term deposits
items.quote: we're expecting a deposit growth between 10% to 12% with a focus on CASA and the retail term deposit

items.statement: FY25 advances growth guided at 12-14% with retail >20% and corporate 11-12%
items.quote: On the advances growth, we are looking at 12% to 14% with a focus on retailising the book more, with retail as such growing at more than 20% and with a corporate growing almost 11% to 12%.

items.statement: FY25 NIM guidance maintained at 3.15% +/- 5 bps on normalized basis
items.quote: We are maintaining our guidance of NIM at 3.15% plus minus 5 bps, but as the market outlook would change then we will just see going forward whether we need revise the guidance.

items.statement: FY25 ROA guidance revised upward from >1% to 1.10%
items.quote: We are revising the guidance upward from 1% to 1.10%. So, considering the strong profit matrix we do have, we are fairly confident that we will achieve a full year ROA of 1.10%.

items.statement: FY25 slippage ratio guidance maintained at 1-1.25%
items.quote: On the slippage ratio, we continue to have the same guidance of 1 to 1.25%.

items.statement: FY25 credit cost guidance maintained at less than 1%
items.quote: The credit cost continues to be, it is already less than 1%, continue to have the same guidance of less than 1%.

items.statement: FY25 NPA recovery target set at Rs 10,000 crore
items.quote: As far as guidance as against 12,000 crore of recovery guidance we had last year, we have announced to the market that 10,000 is the recovery target.

items.quote: Our NIM for the quarter has printed very smartly at 3.27%. items.statement: Yield on advances up ~100 bps YoY; deposit cost up ~100 bps YoY due to tight liquidity
items.quote: In terms of a yield on advances, our yield on advances grew almost 100 basis points year-on-year. There has been pressure on our deposit cost as the liquidity scenario remains tight. We've seen almost 100 basis point increase in deposit costs as well.

items.statement: GNPA below 3% at 2.92%, NNPA 0.68%, PCR 93.3% including TWO as of March 2024
items.quote: GNPA is below 3% and NNPA is well below 1% at 0.68%. Provision coverage ratio is very comfortable at 93.3% including TWO.

items.quote: Slippage has been below our guidance of 1 to 1.25%, it's been at the lower end of the range. I'd like to draw your attention though it is below our range of 1 to 1.25%. There were two large slippages during the course of the year and even after that this has been below 1%.

items.statement: Collection efficiency sustained at 98%
items.quote: In terms of collection efficiency, we continue to print strongly at 98%.

items.quote: As you said rightly, the account is now 100% provided. Why because apart from the primary, we said earlier the account is heavily collateralized, 1/3rd of the exposure is government guaranteed and the balance also if you look at the coll

items.statement: Personal loan GNPA 1.95% on small book; growth moderated from ~100% to 52% YoY; underwriting strengthened with bureau/consultant input
items.quote: As you said right, the book is small and 1.9% GNPA but we are also looking at, more importantly, the collection efficiency and also the slippage part of the PL book. And these are all within the threshold in terms of the slippage. So absolutely no concern at this stage with regard to any stress building up in the PL book.

items.statement: MSME slippage ratio Q4 2.04% vs 2.57% Q3; NPA recovery Rs 2,655 cr; portfolio highly collateralized with higher yields
items.quote: As far as asset quality is concerned, the slippage ratio, quarter on quarter last quarter it was 2.57%. It's come down to 2.04%. And the recovery also, it's robust in the NPA. NPA recovery in MSME book is 2655 crore.

items.statement: Agri slippages FY24 Rs 2,033 cr vs Rs 2,100 cr FY23; Q4 spike to Rs 917 cr from Rs 540 cr YoY but full year normalized
items.quote: So, as far as Agri slippage is concerned during the year, it is 2033 crores and last year it was 2100 crores. So, there is an increase of around 400 crores in the Agri segment Mr. Debadatta Chand: But on a yearly basis, this is almost normalized

items.quote: In terms of CASA, sequentially our CASA grew at 7.5% though year-on-year it has grown at around 5.5%, this is a little ahead of the peer group that we have been seeing the results coming out in the last few days. items.quote: The second aspect which is important out of this financial result is that, we do have a very strong financial performance and the book is growing at 12.5% to 13% wherein the operating profit has gone up by 15.1% and the net profit has gone up by 26%. items.quote: The operating profit growth has also been supported by the very strong and sustained focus on the non-interest income and if you look at the non-interest income for this year vis-a-vis last year, the growth is almost 40.7% from 10,000 crore, it has gone up to 14,495 crores. items.quote: In international segment, the deposit trails the advances. The more we grow the advances book the more we raise the deposit. items.quote: In terms of percentage to the outstanding standard advances which was at 2.04% as on March 2023, has gone down to 0.92%. So, not only on the GNPA, net NPA, we have seen significant improvement, but also the portfolio which can be at risk also has gone down significantly.

items.statement: GNPA/NNPA trending toward 2.5% and 0.5% respectively over time; no fixed timeline given
items.quote: The trending of GNPA, NNPA would be downward from the current level of 2.92%, although we are not giving a guidance, but the trending would try to move towards 2.5%. Similarly, the net NPA from the 0.68% to 0.5%.

items.quote: the growth in deposit we are expecting at 10% to 12% growth going forward. So, this is on the backdrop of the current market outlook and scenario that we expect the deposit growth to be 10% to 12

items.statement: FY25 NIM guidance 3.15% +/- 5 bps

items.quote: we are improving the ROA guidance from 1 to 1.10% this year.

items.quote: full year recovery last year we said 12,000 and we overachieved 12,000 and this year we are giving 10,000 crores as a recovery.

items.quote: this year we expect around 2500 crore recovery from the NCLT accounts, out of 46,000 crores of the book in NCLT.

items.quote: Our NIM due to seasonal impact on account of strong recoveries in the last quarter has gone up to 3.27%. However, if we normalize for the exceptional recoveries we saw this quarter. The normalized NIM for the quarter would be around 3.15%.

items.quote: The NIM printed for the full year was 3.18%. If you normalize for exceptionally strong recoveries in the last quarter, the NIM for the full year would be around 3.14%.

items.statement: GNPA reduced to 2.92%, NNPA 0.68%, PCR 93.3%
items.quote: In terms of GNPA, we have reduced our GNPA to below 3%. Our NNPA is at 0.68%. Our provision coverage ratio is very strong at 93.3%.

items.quote: Slippage is within the range we had given. We had said slippage would be between 1 to 1.25% and we are below the lower end of that band.

items.statement: SMA 1&2 above 5 crore at 0.15% of standard advances
items.quote: In terms of the SMA 1 & 2 above 5 crores, this has been continuously trending downward and that demonstrates that in case of our large ticket loans, there is very little incipient stress at this point in time because there's only 0.15% of those loans which are noncurrent.

items.statement: Collection efficiency 98%
items.quote: In terms of collection efficiency, collections continue to be strong at 98%.

items.statement: Portfolio at risk (SMA 1&2 + restructured) down to 0.92% from 2.04%
items.quote: the portfolio at risk, which I talk about that is the SMA 1 & 2 as per the CRILC report and also the restructured standard book, it has gone down as a percentage of standard advances, which were at 2.04% in the last financial year has gone down to 0.92% this year.

items.statement: CET1 ratio 12.54%, above internal 12% threshold
items.quote: Our CET 1 is very strong at 12.54%, which is above the threshold we have set for ourselves internally, at around 12%.

items.quote: LCR remains healthy at around close to 121%.

items.quote: if you talk about, I mean, the growth almost 12% and I'm at a book of almost three lakh eighty thousand crore on the corporate book. Right.
