Since we will venture into PETCHEM and we also have more plans which is queued towards MS maximization, so within that 77% MS share will marginally go up and diesel share will marginally come down.

items.quote: No. Small correction. Windfall tax is pegged at a defined value of or the price of the crude oil. It has got nothing to do with production. The production component is there and that 20% premium on the gas point. items.quote: Okay and for gas, if you can remind us that 20% premium that you're talking about now your competitor has an opinion that there is no cap applicable on that. Is that an opinion that you also hold which means simply the extra gas that you produce will be sold at a 12% slope instead of a 10% slope

items.statement: Oil India Green Energy Subsidiary creation in approval stage for biofuels, green hydrogen, renewables, compressed biogas
items.quote: And for which we have already taken a decision of creating a subsidiary called Oil India Green Energy Subsidiary, which is in the approval stage.

items.statement: Highest ever combined oil & gas production 6.54 MMTOE in FY24; crude up 6% to 3.359 MMT, gas 3.182 BCM
items.quote: We have been able to manage, and I must share this with great humility and our efforts towards managing mature oil fields, the natural decline in our old and mature fields through highly successful implementation of improved oil recovery and enhanced oil recovery techniques, and improve our combined oil and gas production to the highest ever (and I am repeating this for your benefit), to the highe

items.statement: Mozambique LNG project under force majeure since 2021; hopeful for restart in later part of 2024 with positive developments
items.quote: Currently due to law and order situation, the project is under Force Majeure but with the recent positive developments in Mozambique, we are hopeful that the project will restart somewhere in the later part of '2024.

items.statement: Mission 4+ targets exclude Mozambique production; domestic only
items.quote: No. The mission that we have outlined for ourselves is from domestic production only. This doesn't include anything from Mozambique.

items.statement: Maharatna status conferred August 2023; Vision 2040 aims to double revenue by 2040 via E&P, downstream, alternative energy
items.quote: OIL's vision to become an integrated energy player is backed by aggressive growth plans aiming to double its revenue by 2040. The growth plans are underpinned by substantial Capex investments, spanning exploration, production, downstream and alternative energy ventures.

items.statement: Management expects MRR potential of INR 14-16 crore from current CAPEX over next couple of months
items.quote: we believe that like the MRR potential with the current CAPEX that we have already done would be of the order of anywhere between like 14 to 16 crores from the current MRR number like we should be able to achieve over like next couple of months.

items.statement: Management targets INR 800 crore CAPEX over next 12 months in ideal scenario
items.quote: In an ideal world, like we would like to end another $100 million or about Rs.800 crores over the next 12 months.

items.statement: CAPEX funding to combine bank financing, leasing, vendor financing and equity raise
items.quote: It's will have to be a combination of things including like financing from banks and leasing partners and vendor financing and some equity raise.

items.statement: Demand for cloud GPU workloads expected to increase as industry shifts to GPU-centric computing
items.quote: The demand is only going to increase as the industry shifts to more cloud GPU centric workloads. That demand is only going to increase in the industry.

items.statement: Differentiation through software capabilities and workload understanding creates long-term value
items.quote: that insight into the workload, that ability to understand the need for the workloads and implementing those in the software. That product differentiation is what creates long-term value for our customers.

items.statement: Customer base includes SMEs, higher education, research, startups and partner ecosystem; no migration imperative observed
items.quote: The nature of our customers like primarily is the four different buckets today. So one is of course, like we have the SME segment, which continues to be our main the bulk of our customers, then we have the higher education and research category, then we are back with a bang with working with a lot of startups today.

items.statement: Revenue primarily from India; focus on EMEA and US markets for international expansion
items.quote: currently, like our focus continues to be in India, although we would obviously not refuse any customers coming from outside as well. So from a focus outside your perspective, like majorly we are focused on the EMEA market and the US market.

items.statement: Team size approximately 140-150; organic hiring continues across technology, marketing and operations
items.quote: Broadly, we have claim to somewhere between 140 to 150 people in the team. So approximately about 150 and we continue to grow the team organically.

items.statement: FY24 EBITDA INR 48 crore with 45% YoY growth; Q4 FY24 EBITDA INR 15 crore with 68% YoY growth
items.quote: EBITDA is 48 crore, representing a growth of 45% on year-on-year basis

items.statement: FY24 revenue INR 95 crore with 43% YoY growth; Q4 FY24 revenue INR 29 crore with 67% YoY growth
items.quote: revenue from operations stood at INR 95 crore representing a growth of around 43% year-on-year basis

items.statement: GPU supply constraints easing; normal integration lead times expected going forward
items.quote: There is always going to be some queue. But it's not going to be the longest queue that we have seen in the past of that type okay, like we are looking at 52 weeks, 56 weeks, 60 weeks and so on. That is not going to be the future.

items.statement: InfiniBand 3.2 Tbps deployed to handle unstructured data at scale for AI/ML workloads
items.quote: the overall idea is that , what is difference between the old world o f the CPU and the storage and the new world of CPU plus GPU plus very high speed panel file system kind of storage and so on

items.statement: Management sees no risk of GPU investment obsolescence; GPU compute shift is irrevocable
items.quote: I don't see there is any risk, the process of going to the GPU is irrevocable. The kind of exponential computing offered by GPU is kind of like really changes the era in which we are operating.

items.statement: Services purchased (data center, power, bandwidth, software licenses) scale with revenue; percentage decreases incrementally with volume
items.quote: So the services would be like in the same proportion as the revenue or a way that they will increase with the revenue in a certain incremental percentage fashion.

items.statement: Right-of-use assets relate to lease-to-own equipment; data center services rented not leased under IndAS 116
items.quote: leasing relate to the equipment and this is all lease to own kind of equipment.

items.statement: Government AI announcements indicate exponential data center capacity growth over next five years
items.quote: one of course that the data center capacity required for artificial intelligence is going to kind of, exponentially grow over next five years or so.

items.statement: Expecting 30% revenue increase in FY25 with PAT margin of 6-6.5%
items.quote: Considering the overall growth in the spice market and our future plans we are expecting a 30% increase in our revenue in FY '25. This strategy is focusing on increasing our brand and PAT margin would be in range of 6% to 6.5% in FY '25.

items.statement: Acquired Vita Green Products for INR7.75 crore including plant, machinery and brand
items.quote: I'm very happy to announce that to cater above both sectors, we recently signed a terms sheet with Vita Green Products Private Limited, which are located at Rajkot, Gujarat.

items.statement: Vita Green peak revenue was INR30 crore in 2021, FY23 revenue INR20 crore, profit INR65 lakh
items.quote: The top peak of the company was in 2021 and that was around INR30 crores. And this company was 100% acquisition base and we have acquired it at INR7.75 crores, including the plant and machinery and brand.

items.statement: 50% of acquisition consideration paid; balance to be paid after fixed assets removed from Vita Green
items.quote: We have paid almost 50% to the company and as I mentioned earlier that we have acquired the plant and machinery and the brand itself, while some fixed assets like land, building are in the name of Vitagreen.

items.statement: No additional capex needed for Vita Green manufacturing capacity; can utilize 70-80% in FY25
items.quote: Yeah, in FY '25, we can utilize more than 70 -80% of Vitagreen. Because Vitagreen has production line of only blended and instant mix. While ground spices are acquired by some vendors, which we are currently providing by Madhusudan Masala. So, I don't think any more capex to be utilized in manufacturing capacity.

items.statement: Blended spices EBITDA margin expected to improve significantly in FY25; current blended margins below 20% vs established players at 20-25%
items.quote: Yeah, it is a fair. So, because after adding the blended spices and instant mix, our EBITDA margin must be improved.

items.statement: Powder/blended spices margins almost double whole spices margins
items.quote: Second question of the margins in whole spices and powder spices is margins were almost double for the powder spices.

items.statement: Spice industry valued at INR1 lakh crore in FY24 growing at 10% CAGR; only 35% branded share
items.quote: The spiciest industry is valued at INR1 lakh crore in FY '24 and is growing at a CAGR of 10%. And the noticeable thing in this industry is that only 35% market share is hold by branded companies.

items.statement: Branded sales share increased to 56% from 47% driving margin expansion
items.quote: The PAT margin was increased because our market share of branded sales in total revenue was increased to 56% from 47%.

items.statement: Vita Green adds 228 SKUs (mostly small INR5/10 packets) taking combined portfolio to 500+ SKUs
items.quote: They have 228 SKUs in their product portfolio and we at Madhusudan Masala have 272 SKUs. So our SKUs portfolio will be more than 500 after this acquisition.

items.statement: Vita Green distribution network covers Gujarat, Maharashtra, Goa, Telangana, Punjab, Jammu & Kashmir; 19 million small SKUs sold annually
items.quote: The main strong factor of this company is that their super scopes and distributed network are widely spreaded in Gujarat, Maharashtra, Goa, Telangana, Punjab, and Jammu, Kashmir.

items.statement: Targeting HoReCa segment for whole spices with consistent quality supply
items.quote: So, the main concern for that is to quality that lose whole spices are not coming in consistent quality and we are supplying them consistent quality to all these HoReCa business.

items.statement: Working capital requirement 40-45% of turnover; inventory INR40-45 crore at INR160 crore revenue; debt sufficient for INR160-250 crore turnover
items.quote: If you're going to see our balance sheet, in the financial year '26, there is almost INR20 crores to INR25 crores stock is maintained on an average. But as of now, we have reached to the turnover of the 160, we have to maintain at least INR40 to INR45 crores of stock.

items.statement: 70% of raw material procured in season to ensure consistent quality year-round
items.quote: So, we procure our required procurement was 70% procurement was done in respected season only.

items.statement: Current debt level sufficient for INR160-250 crore turnover; will increase if turnover grows beyond
items.quote: No, no. For this type of INR160 crores to INR250 crores is enough. But in the near future, if turnover is going to be increased indefinitely, that will also increase.

items.statement: Balance 50% acquisition payment from internal accruals and promoter unsecured loans
items.quote: Yeah. Also, some amount from internal actuals and some will be coming by way of unsecured loan from promoters.

items.statement: Installed capacity 2400 metric tons; chili powder at 62% utilization; turmeric/coriander have sufficient capacity
items.quote: No, as of now, I don't think we have to increase our capacity, production capacity, because we have almost 2400 metric ton capacity installed in our unit. And turmeric coriander has more than sufficient capacity we have.

items.statement: Turmeric sourced from Maharashtra; sometimes procure semi-finished powder instead of raw dry turmeric for cost reasons
items.quote: No, because turmeric, we are sourcing turmeric from Maharashtra. So, sometimes it happens that if we procure raw, dry turmeric instead of powdered turmeric, it costs more than a powder product.

items.statement: Only papad, soya chunks and asafoetida procured from vendors; all other products manufactured in-house
items.quote: No. We have all products manufactured in -house, but except three products, like papad, soya chunks, and Asafoetida. Three products are procured directly from vendors and we repaid the change.

items.statement: Products listed on Amazon and JioMart; own e-commerce website generating good numbers; margins similar to offline after returns
items.quote: Yeah, Disha, we have already placed our products in Amazon and JioMart and already started this selling from these two platforms and also trying to place our products in more e-commerce platforms and quick commerce.

items.statement: Targeting unorganized market (65% share) not competing with established brands; using consumer/retail schemes for retention
items.quote: As of now, you see the spices industry has very big numbers in India, like powder spices has INR1 lakh crores in FY '24. But you can see only 35% market share was acquired by branded companies. So, our main concern was not to compete with existing established players. We are targeting unorganized market, which are not any good brand or loose sales.

items.statement: Retail prices lower than established players; offer good trade margins and schemes instead of price cuts
items.quote: No, we are offering good margins to our sales channels and our retail price for consumers are also lower from established players. So, to affect the retail consumers also.

items.statement: Marketing plan includes August 2024 Mumbai exhibition, shop signage, social media, local cable ads, product blend localization
items.quote: We have planned one exhibition in August 24 at Mumbai called [Anugapur 21:22] for acquiring new distributors, super stockists to our western region. And another step is to deploy a shop Asia to our retailers and some social media marketing are also planned.

items.statement: Northern expansion using Vita Green's existing distributors in UP, Bihar, Jharkhand; Madhya Pradesh/Rajasthan need new channels
items.quote: Because these regions were already sold by Vitagreen earlier from last 10 years. So we appointed the same distributors of Vitagreen to Madhusudan. That's why these states are covered because middle states like Madhya Pradesh, Rajasthan are left because Vitagreen do not have sales channels in this part.

items.statement: FY24 revenue grew 28% to INR162 crore; PAT grew 60% to INR9.2 crore
items.value: INR162 crore revenue; INR9.2 crore PAT
items.quote: Our top line revenue was grown by 28% to INR162 crores, while our profit after tax has tremendously increase by 60% to INR9.2 crores.

items.statement: Targeting to double revenue in FY25 from FY24's ₹42.13 crore
items.quote: for the current year, we are thinking of at least doing double of what we did last year

items.statement: Five-year revenue target of ₹500 crore from IPO plan
items.quote: overall five-year plan was of ₹500 crores

items.statement: Total Ambethi plant CapEx of ₹11.5 crore supports up to ₹250 crore revenue
items.quote: we have done almost the entire project is more than ₹11.5 crores in totality. And the overall capacity, if I talk of, so up to ₹250 crores worth of business, we are sure that this particular CapEx will give us the results

items.statement: Expected payback period of 3.5 to 5 years on Ambethi CapEx
items.quote: We are expecting anything between 3.5 to 5 years

items.statement: Ambethi plant currently at 40% utilisation with 36,500 MT powder and 8,000 MT liquid capacity
items.quote: currently, we are utilising only 40% of the plant

items.statement: Liquid capacity utilisation expected to reach 65-70% with admixture and paint focus
items.quote: almost more than 65 % to 70% will be utilised, if we focus on admixture and paint both put together

items.statement: Operating margin improved to 12.6% in FY24 from 8.6% in FY23; expects further 4-5% improvement over time
items.quote: EBITDA has gone to 12.6%, which is again increased

items.statement: Operating margin improvement of 4-5% possible versus organised peers like Sika
items.quote: there is a scope of improvement maybe another 4%, 5%

items.statement: Top 4 product groups (ready mix mortar 42%, tile adhesive/grout 21%, concrete repair 11%, waterproofing 6%) contribute >80% of sales
items.quote: if this top four product groups we put together, it's more than 80% of the sale that we are talking of

items.statement: Admixtures at 2% of sales targeting 8% in FY25; MAARVEL Paints at 3% growing fast
items.quote: this year we are hopeful that we will do almost 8% of our contribution from the Admixture segment

items.statement: Top 10 distributors contribute ~60% of total sales
items.quote: the Top 10 customers are most of the time distributors only. And they contribute to almost 60% of the total sale

items.statement: Related party sales targeted to reduce from current level to ≤25% of sales in FY25, then 20%, 15%
items.quote: the current year, we are targeting that not more than 25% of our overall sales has to come from a related party

items.statement: Construction chemical industry growing at 13.44% CAGR; market expected to double in 5 years from $2.3B to $4.3B
items.quote: going to double in the next five years. So that talks of how big the industry is. And, again, there are so many big players coming into the industry

items.statement: Targeting export markets in Nepal and Bangladesh but prioritising domestic growth first
items.quote: We are also targeting the export market of Nepal and Bangladesh. So but that we are taking a bit slow because looking at the current Indian market itself has got a huge, huge potential

items.statement: Aiming for 60:40 Western zone vs Rest of India revenue mix in 3 years
items.quote: three years down the line, we are expecting 60:40. Western to Rest of India

items.statement: Expanding to South (Karnataka, Telangana) and North (Delhi NCR, UP) with 3-4 distributors already in South, Agra and Ghaziabad in North
items.quote: By end of this financial year, we are planning to have

items.statement: Sales primarily through distributors (8-12% margin) to secure payment cycles and local reach
items.quote: distributors margin, they range between 8 % to 12%. Depending on the turnovers and the schemes that we offer everything put together. The benefit, number one is the payment cycle

items.statement: Raw material (polymer) price spikes are industry-wide and can be passed through to distributors and end customers
items.quote: that kind of spikes are not only for us, they are throughout the industry. So most of the people have to rise the pricing and distributors are ready to accept

items.statement: Competitive edge from in-house R&D, technical solutions, distributor loyalty, and own manufacturing vs peers' contract manufacturing
items.quote: we have got the expertise of construction chemical. So we are able to give solutions to the customer

items.statement: No formal order book; certain government infra tenders with MCON specified expected post-monsoon
items.quote: we don't have order book as such, but yes, we have got certain tenders where MCON is mentioned and which are going to start, post monsoon

items.statement: FY24 net sales growth 35.7%, EBITDA growth 97.5%, PAT growth 97.4%; 3-year CAGR: sales 47.2%, EBITDA 64.2%, PAT 123%
items.quote: net sales growth is 35.7%. EBITDA has gone to 12.6%, which is again increased. Net profit has gone to 5.3%. So EBITDA growth is 97.5%, and net profit growth is 97.4%

items.statement: Business not significantly affected by macro headwinds due to small market share and large addressable market
items.quote: currently, we are at a very, very, very small proportion of the bigger business. So even if there is certain impact, it directly doesn't impact MCON Rasayan

items.statement: ISI certification for 3 major products (tile adhesive, waterproofing admixture, wall putty); ISO 9001, IGBC certified
items.quote: MCON Rasayan is the only company who has got IS I for three major products, which is tile adhesive, water proofing admixture and wall putty

items.statement: Chikli plant closed; Ambethi (owned) and Sarigam (owned) operational; Phase 3 CapEx focused on R&D lab and office
items.quote: Chikli Plant is not anymore operational, but yes, the other plants are operational. So again, when we talk of plants, the major contributor currently is the Ambethi Plant

items.statement: Repair & rehab segment expected to boom in 8-10 years due to aging concrete stock and climate stress; long-term mix target 70:30 new build:repair
items.quote: 10 years down the line, I would say, like, it would be a 70:30 ratio

items.statement: Targets INR1,000 crore brand sales by FY28, implying 32% CAGR from FY24's INR303 crore
items.quote: Looking ahead, ProV aims to achieve significant growth by FY28, targeting brand sales of INR1,000 crores, up from INR303 crore s in FY24, which translates to a CAGR of 32

items.statement: Targets gross margin of 30% by FY28, up from 17% in FY24
items.quote: In addition to sales growth, we project an improvement in gross margin from 17% in FY24 to 30% by FY28.

items.statement: FY24 gross margin improved to 17% from 14.5% in FY23; EBITDA grew 54% to INR11.95 crore; PAT grew 96% to INR7.2 crore
items.quote: Our EBITDA has reached INR11.95 crores, which is year -on-year growth of 54%. Our gross margin improved to 17% from 14.5% in last year. Additionally, our profit after tax stood at INR7.2 crores, demonstrating significant year -on-year growth of 96%.

items.quote: Capex in next 2 years --so right now our gross block is around INR9 crores on the capex side and next 2 years we will invest another INR15 crores to INR18 crore s on the capex side. So, we are expanding our facility production facility continuously

items.statement: Targets 30% top-line growth over next 12 months on recruitment and manpower front
items.quote: We have already have had a few contracts that have come our way at the beginning of the year. And that in itself will add to the top line of the organisation. So, I don't see that a 30% upside should be a problem, over the next 12 months.

items.statement: Targets ~3% operating margin in FY25, definitely by FY26
items.quote: We can expect a range of about 3 odd percent in FY'25. That's what we are targeting. But if not '25, '26, definitely.

items.statement: Historical PAT margin ~4%; current dip due to recruitment/IT staffing slowdown and senior hiring
items.quote: We've typically been working with a 4% sort of a PAT margin in the past. It's not just been the past, it's not just been FY'23, but before that also, if you look at it, we were always in the 4 odd percent sort of a range as an organisation.

items.statement: Recruitment and IT staffing revenue declined ~40-42% YoY in FY24
items.quote: So, it's been about a 40%, 42% sort of a decline, Jatin. In terms of absolute numbers in the recruitment and the IT Staffing business.

items.statement: Consolidated EBITDA fell from ₹23.6 cr to ₹9.4 cr in FY24
items.quote: The revenue overall was ₹1,018 crores as compared to ₹768 crores in the previous year, where the EBITDA was ₹23.6 crores to ₹9.4 crores for FY'24.

items.statement: Seeing pickup in IT recruitment mandates from IT services companies and US clients; RFPs and vendor renewals increasing
items.quote: We started getting demand, Jatin. The science for us is the number of open mandates that we are receiving from our customers. And this usually starts with IT services company.

items.statement: Global HR business grew 15-20% in FY24 vs 100% in FY23; US market opening up now
items.quote: year, it's 15%, 20%. Rahil Dasani: Got it. Vidur Gupta: Last financial year, we had grown 100% FY'23

items.statement: New contracts bagged at start of year will contribute ~12-13% top-line growth
items.quote: The contracts that we have bagged will not help us reach a 30% mark, but they will contribute around a 12% to 13 % odd growth in the top line of the organisation.

items.statement: ~₹15 cr deployed for under-construction office premises (short-term loans & advances)
items.quote: So around ₹15 odd crores, Rahil.

items.statement: ₹55 cr of IPO proceeds still unutilised; used for working capital in staffing/engineering contracts
items.quote: So, Rahil we have around ₹55 odd crores of the IPO funds still lying with us.

items.statement: Added sales headcount: Peush Saproo hired as Head of Sales (21 yrs exp) + ~10 member team for RPO/IT staffing
items.quote: We had Mr. Peush Saproo, who's joined us as the Head of Sales for this business. He came in with over 21 years of experience and was with competition heading sale [inaudible ] [0:02:53] grew this team by about 10 members

items.statement: Core team grew to 490 (from 480 in Sep'23); managed headcount 18,875 + 8,279 apprentices
items.quote: Our core headcount was 490 at the end of March '24 as compared to September '23 where the internal headcount was 480 numbers.

items.statement: Electronics trading (mobiles only) to be wound down within FY25; not long-term focus
items.quote: We want to shut it by the end of within this year, not by the end of the year. I'm hoping that we are able to get the other businesses up, and hopefully we'll be able to shut it as soon as possible.

items.statement: Electronics trading grew due to faster capital rotation (3x/month vs usual 2x) in H2
items.quote: There was a lot of turnaround and quick turnaround that happened in the shipments in this H2, where usually, we used to be able to rotate capital twice in the month. However, a number of times, we were able to do it thrice in the last H2.

items.statement: Candidate salary hike expectations dropped from 30-40% to 20-25%, causing offer shopping and lower joining ratios
items.quote: At the moment, the industry is offering more in the range of about 20%, 22%, 25%, which is resulting in a fair amount of retention as well. And a lot of offer shopping, which is why it's not yet corresponding into performance from an organisational standpoint, it will come.

items.statement: Trade receivables ₹78.5 cr includes ~₹10 cr from electronics trading; similar to last year
items.quote: So, trading has some bit of it, Rahi l. I believe it is to the tune of ₹10 odd crores roughly

items.statement: Annual salary cost rose from ~₹14 cr to ~₹22.2 cr (Mar'23 to Mar'24) due to senior hires
items.quote: Annual number, just a second. So, our salary cost has gone up from a ₹14 odd crores to a ₹22.2 odd crores.

items.statement: Achieved Great Place to Work certification in May'24 to attract talent
items.quote: If you did notice, we achieved the great place to work certification also. This came in May this year. We've added it in the presentation.

items.statement: Productivity (managed headcount per core employee) improved from 280 to 348
items.quote: We used, it was previously 280 for the second half of the financial year '23, which is now 348.

items.statement: Manpower supply EBITDA margin 1.1% in H2 vs 1% in H1; electronics trading 0.7% vs 0.9%
items.quote: The EBITDA margin for the manpower supply was 1.1% in the second half of the year as compared to a 1% in the previous half. And the electronic goods, it was 0.7% as compared to 0.9% in the first half of the year.

items.statement: Added 70 new logos in H2; client attrition routine, no significant losses
items.quote: We added 70 new logos in the H2.

items.statement: Client attrition routine; market consolidating as formalisation drives growth across competitors
items.quote: Nothing significant. So, if we are getting, see there are two ways to look at this, Rahil. One, if you look at it, all the firms are growing in terms of size.

items.statement: Industry-wide slowdown in recruitment/IT staffing; peers also seeing margin pressure
items.quote: If you look at the performance of our competition as well, while we don't like to comment on competition, but in general, the industry, there has been a massive slowdown in the Recruitment and the IT Staffing business, which is starting to come up now.

items.statement: RPO contracts take 3 months to close + 2 months implementation; revenue starts month 4-5
items.quote: Agreement takes about three months to close. Post the agreement about two odd months to usually set up and place the team in place. And at the end of those two months, revenue starts to come.

items.statement: Other operating expenses rose from ₹4.4 cr to ₹11.48 cr due to professional staffing fees and job board costs (₹35 lakh)
items.quote: So, Jatin, what has happened is we have been able to bag a contract, which is not a contract staffing assignment, but it is a professional staffing assignment. So, the fee to those professionals has been put in the other operating expenses.
